name: com.doseedo/doseedo
title: Doseedo: Film Scoring, AI Instruments, Sound Effects & Stems
description: Score video, make music as an agent: 100+ AI instruments play your MIDI, audio, stems, Logic/Ableton

tools.name: doseedo_generate_music
tools.description: NOT A COMPOSER: doseedo plays music, it does not write it — YOU write the piece. Background music for a video or a brand film, an instrumental, a theme, a song: compose every part yourself as notes ([{pitch, start_beats, duration_beats, velocity}], beats from bar 1 — melody, harmony, bass, in the key and at the tempo you choose), then play them: doseedo_render_score {parts} for several instruments (one stem each, then doseedo_mix) or doseedo_render_midi for one; doseedo_instruments lists the players and their ranges; the steps: doseedo_recipes name="compose-piece" (to picture: "score-a-film"; one part in a session's key: "compose-part"). THIS tool is text to music from a PROMPT alone (optionally lyrics) with NO notes behind it: the instrument model then has nothing to play, and a take is often near-silent, a drone or clicks. Nothing in it is controlled — no key control (a key in the prompt is not honoured), no MIDI input, bpm/time_signature only tag the caption. Use it only when the user explicitly asks for a prompt-only AI sketch, listen before handing a take over, and never deliver one as the music. Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (typically 1–3 min) → audio URLs (pre-signed: curl -OJ <url>, no auth header, valid 24 h — see expires_at). Cancel: a render that has not reached the GPU yet is stopped and its credits refunded; one already rendering finishes on the GPU (its credits are spent), the job ends as canceled and the output is discarded.

prompt.description: Style/mood/instrumentation prompt, e.g. "warm jazz trio, brushed drums, late-night ballad". ≤ 16000 characters (a longer one is cut at a word boundary, with a warning).

lyrics.description: Optional lyrics to sing, ≤ 16000 characters. Omit for instrumental.

duration_seconds.description: Target length in seconds (e.g. 30–120). Omit for the model default.

bpm.description: Optional tempo HINT in BPM, written into the caption (default 120). Not enforced — the output tempo can drift from it.

time_signature.description: Optional meter HINT written into the caption, e.g. "4/4", "3/4". Not enforced.

name.description: Optional: a name for this job's files, e.g. "rainy-loop-3". Every file it returns downloads as <name>_<part>.<ext> (rainy-loop-3_Celesta.wav, rainy-loop-3_rough-mix.wav; one take: rainy-loop-3.wav), so the user can find them. Give each job its own name (a second take: "rainy-loop-3b"). Default: doseedo-<last 6 characters of the job id>.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_generate_sound
tools.description: SOUND EFFECTS (SFX) from words with Stable Audio Open — SOUND DESIGN and FOLEY for game audio, apps and video: impacts, whooshes, door slams, footsteps, UI blips, creature and sci-fi sounds, ambiences ("rain on a tin roof", "busy café"), risers, drum one-shots. A one-shot hit ("punchy house kick", "snare with a short room", "a riser into the drop"), a loop on the tempo grid ("glitchy percussion"), or a texture ("vinyl crackle", "rain"). kind picks which (hit | loop | texture); omitted, the server reads it off the words. Don't put a tempo in a hit's prompt — tempo words make it write a loop. Wrong tool for a part with notes (doseedo_render_midi) or a piece of music (you write it; doseedo_render_score plays it). Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (typically 15–40 s) → audio URLs (pre-signed: curl -OJ <url>, no auth header, valid 24 h). Each sound is one 30 s window = 10 credits: before sending a batch, doseedo_quote {job: "generate_sound"} or doseedo_account says how many the account has room for now. Cancel: a render that has not reached the GPU yet is stopped and its credits refunded; one already rendering finishes on the GPU (its credits are spent), the job ends as canceled and the output is discarded.

prompt.description: What it sounds like, e.g. "punchy house kick drum, single hit" or "dusty vinyl crackle". ≤ 300 characters (a longer one is cut at a word boundary, with a warning).

kind.description: hit = one sound (0.5–10 s), loop = 1–4 bars tiled at bpm, texture = a bed. Default: read off the prompt.

duration_seconds.description: Length in seconds. Default: 2 s for a hit, 4 bars at bpm for a loop, 8 s for a texture.

bpm.description: Tempo a loop is cut to (default 120).

time_signature.description: Meter a loop is cut to, e.g. "4/4" (default).

name.description: Optional: a name for this job's files, e.g. "rainy-loop-3". Every file it returns downloads as <name>_<part>.<ext> (rainy-loop-3_Celesta.wav, rainy-loop-3_rough-mix.wav; one take: rainy-loop-3.wav), so the user can find them. Give each job its own name (a second take: "rainy-loop-3b"). Default: doseedo-<last 6 characters of the job id>.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_generate_loop
tools.description: A DRUM LOOP from a generator — doseedo_generators lists them (house, deep_house, tech_house, afro_house, jackin_house… the list grows without a release). The groove is WRITTEN for the seed (kick, clap, hats, shaker, percussion voices, ghost notes, fills at the phrase ends, 16th swing) and PLAYED through the generator's kit of recorded one-shots (drawn by the seed, the kick tuned to key): the same generator + seed + bars + bpm is the same loop, another seed another groove and another kit. Returns the loop as audio (48 kHz WAV, exactly `bars` long, its tails wrapped round the loop point so it repeats seamlessly), its MIDI (midi_url, GM drums) and, for a short loop, the notes (notes[] — edit them and play them back with doseedo_render_midi {instrument:"electronic", drum_genre:"<the generator's genre>", notes}, or put them on a session track with set_midi_notes). MIDI only, free and instant: doseedo_generators {generator, bars, bpm, seed}. Wrong tool for drums you wrote (doseedo_render_midi) or a described sound (doseedo_generate_sound). Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (a few seconds) → files[0] (pre-signed: curl -OJ <url>, no auth header, valid 24 h). Cancel: a render that has not reached the GPU yet is stopped and its credits refunded; one already rendering finishes on the GPU (its credits are spent), the job ends as canceled and the output is discarded.

generator.description: REQUIRED. A generator id from doseedo_generators ("deep_house", "tech_house"…) or genre words that name one ("afro house"). An unknown one is refused with the closest ids before anything is spent.

bars.description: Length in bars of 4/4, 1–64. Default: the generator's (8).

bpm.description: Tempo, 40–240. Default: the generator's own (house 124, deep 120, tech 127…).

seed.description: The groove and the kit: the same seed is the same loop; omit for a new one each call (the result names it).

key.description: The track's key, e.g. "F minor" — the kick is drawn near its root or fifth and tuned the rest of the way.

swing.description: 16th swing: 0.5 straight … 0.66 triplet. Default: the generator's.

fills.description: false = no fills at the phrase ends (a loop that sits under a verse). Default true.

percussion.description: How many percussion voices (0–4). Default: the generator draws it.

name.description: Optional: a name for this job's files, e.g. "rainy-loop-3". Every file it returns downloads as <name>_<part>.<ext> (rainy-loop-3_Celesta.wav, rainy-loop-3_rough-mix.wav; one take: rainy-loop-3.wav), so the user can find them. Give each job its own name (a second take: "rainy-loop-3b"). Default: doseedo-<last 6 characters of the job id>.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_cover_stem
tools.description: TIMBRE TRANSFER (an instrument swap) from a recording: hum or whistle a melody, play it on a kazoo, take a guitar line — and get it back played by a cello, a trumpet, a koto (any doseedo_instruments call). Re-play ONE recorded part — a separated stem, a solo, a region of the user's session — on another instrument, straight from the audio: the recording's FSQ codes carry its structure into a take generated from noise, and the sound is the instrument's (caption + timbre_preset) — the FSQ + timbre combination the cond5 model was trained on (served on its turbo graft). No MIDI by default (midi:true adds the server's own pitch roll of the recording); `fidelity` > 0 also keeps that much of the recording's own latents (closer, but its sound leaks back in). For the exact notes, transcribe and doseedo_render_midi; a whole mix → doseedo_cover_song. result.recipe says what reached the model (fsq, timbre, cns). Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (~30–90 s) → takes[{url}] (pre-signed: curl -OJ, no auth header, 24 h). Cancel: a render that has not reached the GPU yet is stopped and its credits refunded; one already rendering finishes on the GPU (its credits are spent), the job ends as canceled and the output is discarded.

audio_key.description: R2 ingest key of an uploaded audio file (from doseedo_get_upload_url / POST /api/upload/r2/ingest-url; starts with "ingest/"). Provide this, audio_url, or latent_key.

audio_url.description: https URL of the audio, as an alternative to audio_key: a doseedo result URL exactly as a job returned it (a stem, a take, a bounce), or any public URL. The gateway fetches it (≤256 MB) into your account's ingest storage before the job starts. Pass audio_key OR audio_url.

latent_key.description: Instead of the audio: the recording already VAE-encoded (ACE-Step 1.5 VAE, 48 kHz stereo → [T, 64] at 25 Hz, the latent mean) as a 64-channel 25 Hz float WAV `*.latent.wav`, uploaded like audio (POST /api/jobs/uploads). The server skips its encode. Dø Desktop sends this when encoding on the Mac lands sooner than uploading the audio.

instrument.description: REQUIRED. The instrument that plays it — call.instrument from doseedo_instruments (with its call.timbre_preset where it has one).

timbre_preset.description: A named timbre preset (the catalog's preset ids, e.g. "cello:preset1"). Omit for the instrument default.

duration_seconds.description: REQUIRED. The recording's length in seconds (0.5–600): the take is this long.

fidelity.description: How much of the recording's own latents the take keeps, 0–0.6 (cover noise strength over the source). Default 0: structure from its FSQ codes only, the sound all the instrument's.

midi.description: true = the server also transcribes the recording's notes into a roll that drives the MIDI hooks beside the FSQ codes — closer notes, a little slower (LatentPitch on audio; vaescriptor on a latent_key; a drum part — either route — gets its hits from vaescriptor_drums). recipe.midi_source names it. Default false: the codes alone.

fsq.description: false = leave the recording's FSQ codes out: the take follows the server's note roll (needs midi: true) on the instrument's sound, with none of the source's phrasing or articulation carried over — for a line whose phrasing doesn't suit the new instrument (a sung vocal on a sax). Default true. recipe.fsq says which ran.

lyrics.description: A SINGER's cover (instrument "voice" or "choir" — doseedo_instruments rows with sings:true): the words to sing, a line per phrase, in the order the recording sings them — e.g. the recording's own words transcribed. The take sings them in the recording's phrasing (its FSQ codes). ≤2000 chars. Without it a singer sings no words. Any other instrument: an error.

takes.description: How many takes, 1–4 (default: the server's best-of-N).

name.description: Optional: a name for this job's files, e.g. "rainy-loop-3". Every file it returns downloads as <name>_<part>.<ext> (rainy-loop-3_Celesta.wav, rainy-loop-3_rough-mix.wav; one take: rainy-loop-3.wav), so the user can find them. Give each job its own name (a second take: "rainy-loop-3b"). Default: doseedo-<last 6 characters of the job id>.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_edit_lyrics
tools.description: LYRIC EDIT / VOCAL INPAINT: send a sung recording and its words as they should be, and get the recording back with the changed words sung in the SAME singer's voice on the same melody — punched in: every word left alone plays as recorded (bit-exact), only the changed words (with a word of context) are sung again and spliced in. A whole song works too: its vocal is separated, edited and mixed back into the song (vocal_only: true skips that for a vocal on its own). Best with `heard` — the recording's words with their times, as you heard them (Whisper): send EVERY heard line in `lyrics`, the ones to change in their new words, and each line is laid on its own phrase, changed word by word. Without it the server hears the words itself and matches your lines to its phrases. Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (~60–180 s) → takes[{url}] as long as the recording (pre-signed: curl -OJ, no auth header, 24 h); output.lyric_edit says what was heard, what was sung again where (splice), and the credits it settled. Cancel: a render that has not reached the GPU yet is stopped and its credits refunded; one already rendering finishes on the GPU (its credits are spent), the job ends as canceled and the output is discarded.

audio_key.description: R2 ingest key of an uploaded audio file (from doseedo_get_upload_url / POST /api/upload/r2/ingest-url; starts with "ingest/"). Provide this or audio_url.

audio_url.description: https URL of the audio, as an alternative to audio_key: a doseedo result URL exactly as a job returned it (a stem, a take, a bounce), or any public URL. The gateway fetches it (≤256 MB) into your account's ingest storage before the job starts. Pass audio_key OR audio_url.

lyrics.description: REQUIRED. The words as they should be sung, a line per phrase in the recording's order. With `heard`: every heard line, one each, the lines to change in their new words (a line left as heard is not sung again).

heard.description: The recording's words as heard (e.g. Whisper word timestamps), so the edit lands exactly where they are sung: {text: the heard lines joined by "\n", words: [{word, start, end}] in seconds of the audio sent}. A line of `text` is a phrase; `lyrics` then sends one line per phrase.

duration_seconds.description: REQUIRED. The recording's length in seconds (0.5–600).

notes.description: The new words placed NOTE BY NOTE, as an editor shows a vocal: the recording's melody as notes (e.g. the transcribe job's, instrument "voice") in seconds of the audio sent, each note to sing again carrying its `lyric` — "glo-" (more of the word follows), "a", a whole word, "_" (hold the syllable before) or "" (sing nothing there). A note without `lyric` plays as recorded. Only the runs of notes with a lyric are sung again — those syllables on those notes, exactly — and spliced in; `lyrics` is then just the words they sing.

vocal_gender.description: The singer's voice, a hint for the vocal model (default: heard from the recording).

vocal_only.description: true = the recording is a vocal on its own: never separated (a DAW's vocal track). Default: the server checks — a song's vocal is separated, edited and mixed back.

name.description: Optional: a name for this job's files, e.g. "rainy-loop-3". Every file it returns downloads as <name>_<part>.<ext> (rainy-loop-3_Celesta.wav, rainy-loop-3_rough-mix.wav; one take: rainy-loop-3.wav), so the user can find them. Give each job its own name (a second take: "rainy-loop-3b"). Default: doseedo-<last 6 characters of the job id>.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_fill_gap
tools.description: INPAINT (repair) a part: send ONE recorded part (a stem, a DAW track's audio) with a gap in it — the silence between two clips, a bar to redo, a dropout — and get it back with the gap PLAYED: the take before and after the gap is kept bit-exact (spliced back), and the gap is generated against both, so it continues out of what comes before and leads into what follows. What fills it is planned first (the DSP plane's extend planner, which hears the part): the take's own LOOP when it has one — the gap is seeded from its own passes at the matching bar phase, so a groove keeps turning — else a part written in its key and over its chords, performed in the take's own sound. Pass the session's bpm and bar grid (bar_offset_seconds: where a bar line falls in the audio you send); the gap is in seconds of that audio. Send the part with some of the take on each side of the gap (8 bars or more before it is best). Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (~40–150 s) → takes[{url}]: WAVs as long as the audio you sent, the gap filled — cut out the gap (or the span you need) to drop it into the DAW. output.plan says what filled it (loop bars, or the writer and the changes). Cancel: a render that has not reached the GPU yet is stopped and its credits refunded; one already rendering finishes on the GPU (its credits are spent), the job ends as canceled and the output is discarded.

audio_key.description: R2 ingest key of an uploaded audio file (from doseedo_get_upload_url / POST /api/upload/r2/ingest-url; starts with "ingest/"). The part, with the gap in it. Provide this or audio_url.

audio_url.description: https URL of the audio, as an alternative to audio_key: a doseedo result URL exactly as a job returned it (a stem, a take, a bounce), or any public URL. The gateway fetches it (≤256 MB) into your account's ingest storage before the job starts. Pass audio_key OR audio_url.

duration_seconds.description: REQUIRED. The audio's length in seconds (1–600).

gap_start_seconds.description: REQUIRED. Where the gap starts, in seconds of the audio.

gap_end_seconds.description: REQUIRED. Where the gap ends (and the take resumes), in seconds of the audio.

bpm.description: REQUIRED. The session's tempo — the gap is filled on its bar grid.

bar_offset_seconds.description: Where a bar line falls in the audio (seconds; default 0 = the audio starts on a downbeat). Sending a span of a DAW track that starts mid-bar? Give the first downbeat's time in it.

exact_grid.description: true = the audio is cut from a DAW session, so bpm and bar_offset_seconds are its EXACT grid: the fill keeps it (default false: the planner fine-tunes the grid to the audio's own onsets — right for a stem whose tempo you only know roughly).

fill.description: What fills the gap: "context" = the span played AGAIN from the take around it — no plan, no notes: a variation of what is there, in its own sound and level (INPAINTING a span that has audio — the right default there); "loop" = the take's own passes (a groove that keeps turning), "written" = a part written in its key and chords, "auto" (default) = the loop when the part has one, else written.

keep.description: fill "context": how much of what is in the span its regeneration keeps, 0.01–0.9 (default 0.05: a variation; 0.45 ≈ the same playing again).

notes.description: YOUR part for the gap — a custom part (a MIDI region drawn there in the DAW): [{pitch, start_seconds, duration_seconds, velocity?}], seconds of the audio you send. It is the written part, no planner: the take plays exactly these notes, in its own sound (notes outside the gap are ignored; silence where there are none). fill "written" or omitted. ≤2000.

instrument.description: What plays the part (an id from doseedo_instruments). Optional — the take's own sound is kept either way; a written fill is played by it.

role.description: The part's role, when you know it (the planner hears it otherwise).

track_name.description: The part's track name in the DAW ("Drums", "Bass", "Strings") — the planner hears a role from the name first, then from the sound.

takes.description: How many takes, 1–4 (default: the server's best-of-N).

seed.description: Optional random seed (the same seed plans and renders the same).

name.description: Optional: a name for this job's files, e.g. "rainy-loop-3". Every file it returns downloads as <name>_<part>.<ext> (rainy-loop-3_Celesta.wav, rainy-loop-3_rough-mix.wav; one take: rainy-loop-3.wav), so the user can find them. Give each job its own name (a second take: "rainy-loop-3b"). Default: doseedo-<last 6 characters of the job id>.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_render_midi
tools.description: MIDI to audio, a virtual instrument: plays a part you wrote. An AI instrument model (orchestral strings, brass, woodwinds, piano, guitar, bass, drums, World) performs your exact notes, in your key, at your bpm, and returns audio takes. Input ONE of: notes[] ({pitch, start_beats, duration_beats, velocity} — beats from bar 1), midi_url (a .mid ≤2 MiB: a doseedo result link or a public https URL), or session_id + track_id (that track's notes, read from the session). Required: instrument (an entry's `call` from doseedo_instruments, no key — stay inside its range) and bpm. The notes are sent AS GIVEN — no pitch snapping, no quantizing. One voice per part: a chord part is rendered one voice per output with voice_split:true (result.voices maps each voice to its files and notes). Takes come back best-first (takes[0] = the scorer's winner). Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (~1–3 min). Result: takes[{url, rank, score}] (pre-signed: curl -OJ, no auth header, 24 h), seed, duration, voices?, refine?, chain. A take may miss or change a note — read takes[].check (measured against your notes) or listen; offer the takes, never promise note-perfection. Free harmony check first: doseedo_analyze_midi. DRUMS (GM notes): the drum model (default) PLAYS a kit — the sound of acoustic drums; it can drop a hit (takes[].fit.missing). drum_engine:"oneshot" = a programmed sampler kit for drum_genre (default for "electronic"/"808"), every hit as written — drum machines only; real drums (a kit, boom bap) stay on the model (drop a hit: take again). "synth" = a one-shot patch (synth_role, synth_genre; "performed" = played, less 1-shot); result.oneshots = the samples. SOUND: a preset (timbre_preset), a recording's tone (timbre_audio_url = timbre transfer; a drum kit too: a ride / snare recording), or YOUR OWN instrument (lora_id from doseedo_train_instrument; result.lora.applied). Cancel: a render that has not reached the GPU yet is stopped and its credits refunded; one already rendering finishes on the GPU (its credits are spent), the job ends as canceled and the output is discarded.

notes.description: The part, as note rows in beats from bar 1 (beat 0 = bar 1 beat 1, quarter-note beats at `bpm`). Monophonic for one voice; chords need voice_split:true. Up to 4096 notes.

lyric.description: A SUNG part (instrument "voice" or "choir"): the syllable this note sings — "glo-" (more of the word follows), "a", a whole word, or "_" to hold the previous syllable over this note. Placed exactly (wins over `lyrics`); a note without one sings no word of its own.

midi_url.description: Alternative to notes: https URL of a Standard MIDI File (≤2 MiB) — a doseedo result link (a stem's MIDI) or a public URL. Its own tempo map is used by the model; bpm still tags the caption and sizes the default duration.

session_id.description: Alternative to notes: with track_id, render THAT session track's notes (read from doseedo_get_session's summary).

track_id.description: With session_id: the t_… id of the MIDI/instrument track to render.

instrument.description: REQUIRED. The instrument from doseedo_instruments — its `call.instrument` (e.g. "violin", "tenor_sax", "electric_guitar", "piano"; a World name such as "koto" is resolved to its call). Keep the notes inside its range. An unknown name close to a catalog one is refused with did_you_mean before anything is spent.

bpm.description: REQUIRED (or tempo_map). Tempo of the notes (10–400). Written into the MIDI's tempo meta, so start_beats/duration_beats land at exactly this tempo.

tempo_map.description: Tempo CHANGES for the notes: [{beat, bpm}] — each point holds from its beat (beats from bar 1) until the next; the first point is beat 0 (or bpm covers the beats before it). Written into the MIDI, so a ritardando or a tempo that lands a cue on a film hit plays exactly. doseedo_tempo_map builds one from hit times.

revise_take_url.description: REVISE an earlier take instead of rendering a new one: the take's URL (as a render returned it). Only [revise_start_beats, revise_end_beats) is regenerated — steered by `notes` (send the whole part, with your corrections) — and spliced back with short crossfades; the rest of the take is kept as it was.

revise_start_beats.description: With revise_take_url: start of the region to redo, beats from bar 1.

revise_end_beats.description: With revise_take_url: end of the region to redo (exclusive), beats from bar 1.

time_signature.description: Meter of the part, e.g. "4/4", "3/4", "6/8" (default 4/4). Written into the MIDI and the caption.

duration_seconds.description: Length of the render in seconds (0.01–600). Default: the last note's end + 2 s of release. Each 30 s window costs 10 credits.

takes.description: How many takes to render, 1–4 (one GPU batch; no extra credits). Omit to let the server choose best-of-N for the part length.

seed.description: Random seed (−1 or 0–4294967295). Reuse a result's seed to re-render close to the same take.

lyrics.description: A SUNG part (instrument "voice" — a solo singer — or "choir"): the words, one syllable per note in time order ("Hold the light a lit-tle lon-ger": hyphens split a word where you want, "_" holds a syllable over the next note; one word such as "Ah" is sung on every note). ≤ 2000 characters. Without it a sung part sings "Ooh". Any other instrument: an error.

timbre_preset.description: A preset from doseedo_instruments — an entry's call.timbre_preset or presets[].call.timbre_preset (e.g. "violin:pizz", "sax:alto", "koto:preset1"). Omit for the instrument default.

timbre_audio_url.description: TIMBRE TRANSFER: https URL of a short recording (≤24 MB; its first 30 s are used) whose SOUND the render should take on — a doseedo result link or a public URL. The notes stay yours; the tone comes from the recording. A VOICE only with consent: the user's own, or a singer who agreed to it (doseedo's Terms) — never to imitate a real artist or anyone else without their permission.

lora_id.description: A CUSTOM INSTRUMENT: the lora_id doseedo_train_instrument returned (16 hex). The render is played by that trained instrument; pass the same instrument it was trained as. Owner-only.

lora_strength.description: With lora_id (or synth_engine "performed"): how strongly the custom instrument applies, 0–2 (default 1.0, or a tuned per-adapter default; ~0.6 when a small training set overshoots; performed synth 0.5 — up to ~0.75 plays it looser, past that it starts leaving the notes).

voice_split.description: true = the notes hold chords: split them into the voices one player of this instrument can hold and render every voice (result.voices). A SUNG chord (choir, voice) is sung one stem per voice, each in its register, one take each. Default false (a chord in a mono part is an error the model will fudge).

refine.description: Opt-in post-render correction. "light": attacks re-timed onto the score, exposed wrong pitch classes re-pitched inside the played octave, misfires muted (winds/brass/strings). "shred": play exactly the written line, octave included, mute anything the score never wrote (any pitched mono part). The raw render stays downloadable (result.refine.raw_url).

dynamics.description: One target dynamic for the whole part's tone: "pp", "p", "mp", "mf", "f", "ff", "fff", a 0–1 number, or a MIDI velocity as text. Omit it to let the notes' velocities shape the tone (dynamics_curve).

tune.description: Light intonation (default true): a held, clearly pitched note the model rendered 15–85 cents off its written pitch is moved toward it, to a small natural residual — attack and vibrato as played, fast notes left. Winds, brass and strings. false = the take exactly as rendered.

band_decode.description: ON by default (false = the plain decode) for every instrument the band decoder table gives a model — guitars (acoustic, electric, nylon), acoustic and electric piano, cello, arco double bass: the take's 1–7 kHz rebuilt from its own latent by the band model, so the partials above 1 kHz keep their fine structure (a plain decode keeps their level and loses it). Any other instrument keeps the plain decode. ~0.7 s per 30 s take on a warm GPU (the first decode with a model on a GPU adds ~15 s, once). Receipt: band_decode {applied, decodes (model:family → decodes), table, ms, why_not}.

vaefix.description: VAE spectral corrector (default true): trims the low-mid fog the decoder adds under the instrument's register and removes mic hiss only when the take carries it. Winds, brass and strings. Receipt: vaefix. false = the decode exactly as rendered.

dynamics_curve.description: What colours the TONE over time: omitted/"auto" = the note velocities when they vary (soft notes darker, loud brighter — every instrument but drums, LoRAs included); "off" = one colour; "cc11"/"cc1" = that CC lane of a midi_url; or "pos:level,…" (pos and level 0–1, e.g. "0:0.1,1:0.9" = a crescendo). Receipt: result.dynamics.

drum_genre.description: The drum style. A drum machine (instrument "electronic" or "808"): the genre whose one-shot kit plays the part — "house", "techno", "trap", "drill", "dnb", "amapiano", "synthwave"… or free words. "tech" = the modern product-film sound (trap / electronic / pop, clean and minimal): a synthesized drum machine, its kick tuned to `key`, nothing generated. A real-drums style ("boom bap", "lo-fi", "breakbeat", "funk", "rock", "jazz"…) plays on the drum model's drum_kit instead, never a one-shot kit. Default: the instrument.

drum_engine.description: Who plays a drum part: "model" = the drum model (the default for every kit but electronic / 808): a drummer playing the kit in a room — cymbals ring, hits vary, ghost notes speak; the sound for acoustic drums. It can drop or smear a hit: read takes[].fit and take it again. "oneshot" = a sampler kit made for drum_genre (the default for electronic / 808; congas and bongos are recordings of the skins): every note lands exactly as written, but it sounds programmed (one sample per drum, the same on every hit) — for drum-machine genres only. An acoustic kit (drum_kit: rock, punk, jazz, soul, a band seen playing) stays on the model, never oneshot — and so does a real-drums drum_genre on whatever kit, which plays on drum_kit (funk, boom bap, lo-fi, breakbeat: a sampled break is a drummer; its dust comes from the mix, doseedo_mix style "1990s-hiphop" / "lofi-hiphop"; the submit reply says so, prepared.drums). A take that drops a hit is taken again (takes: 3, keep the best). Its pads (GM): kick 35/36, snare 38/40, rim 37, clap 39, hats 42/44/46, toms 41–50, crash 49/57, ride 51/59, tambourine 54, cowbell 56, bongos 60/61, congas 62–64, shaker 69/70/82, guiro 73/74, claves 75, woodblock 76/77, triangle 80/81.

synth_role.description: instrument "synth": the patch Stable Audio Open makes for the part — bass (an 808 where the genre's bass is one), 808, pad, lead, pluck. Default: from the notes (chords = pad, a low line = bass, else lead).

synth_genre.description: instrument "synth": the genre the patch is made for — "house", "techno", "trap", "synthwave", "lo-fi", "dnb"… or free words. "tech" = the modern product-film sound: a computed synth voice (a sine sub that glides, a dark pluck, a filtered pad), exactly in tune, every note as written — synth_words still turn it ("dark", "bright", "driven", "short", "wide").

key.description: The music's key ("D minor", "F#", "Bb major"). A synthesized drum machine (drum_genre "tech") tunes its kick and toms to it.

synth_words.description: instrument "synth": extra sound words for the patch ("reese", "warm analog", "acid"), ≤ 80 characters (a longer one is cut at a word boundary, with a warning).

synth_patch.description: instrument "synth": a SAMPLED patch in place of the genre's computed voice — recorded notes played by a sampler, every note as written. "<pack>:<patch>": a hardware synth preset by id or name ("xv5080:PR-C/056", "xv5080:JUNO Strings"), or a pitched pack by name ("bass808" = a recorded 808, chosen by synth_words: long / short, deep / distorted). A patch the server cannot read plays the computed voice (the receipt's synth_engine says which).

synth_engine.description: Who plays a synth part: "oneshot" = a patch of one-shots made for it (the default for "synth"; every note the same sample), "performed" = that same patch (synth_role / synth_genre / synth_words pick it) played by the synth model trained on real synth loops — each note its own, the tone moving, the written notes kept (lora_strength 0.5 default; seed = another performance), and with timbre_audio_url (a reference track's bass / lead / pad stem) the patch is CUT FROM THAT RECORDING's own notes and the synth model performs it — the default for a synth part that brings a recording: your notes, its sound (result.synth_engine.patch_engine "reference-patch"; lora.error = no single note could be cut, the model played it with the recording as its timbre); "oneshot" with timbre_audio_url plays that cut patch exactly as written with no model pass (the default for role 808: the synth model loses a sub's pitches), "model" = the instrument model alone.

prompt.description: Optional caption override (default: the instrument id), ≤ 16000 characters. Style words help a little; the notes are the control.

articulation.description: HOW the part is played, a passage at a time — no per-note work needed: a style for the whole part ("legato"), passages [{from, to, style?, dynamics?}] (beats from bar 1, [from, to)), or {style?, passages?, notes?: [{at, pitch?, style?, vibrato?, hairpin?, curve?, bend?}], curve?: [[beat, dB], …], unit?: "beats"|"seconds"}. Styles: legato tenuto portato staccato staccatissimo spiccato accent marcato sfz fp swell crescendo decrescendo espressivo molto_vibrato senza_vibrato breathy growl bright dark fall doit scoop gliss (aliases: slur, short, >, ^, sf, cresc, dim, subtone, glissando…; a list combines them). A sentence where a name goes ("short, warm, no vibrato") is read for its lengths, vibrato and tone only (receipt described); an accent, a hairpin or a bend is named on its passage or note. dynamics: "mf", or a hairpin over the span "p<f", "f>p", "p<f>p" (ppp…fff). curve = a RELATIVE level curve (±18 dB) added to every note under it: a master / section swell over existing dynamics. Any span or note may also set vibrato, vibrato_rate, bright, breath, rough (0–1) and attack ("slur" | "tongue" | 0–1); a note: hairpin "<" ">" "<>", curve (its level 0–127 through it), bend (semitones through it). Later passages / notes win field by field; curves add. On an instrument with an articulation model (doseedo_instruments articulation) the part plays on that model (vibrato, colour, attacks, in-note shapes); elsewhere lengths, accents, dynamics, curves and bends still apply. On a GUITAR (electric, or a steel-string acoustic) a LINE (a lead, a riff, a fill: one note at a time) plays on its model: bright is the drive (0 clean, straight into the board … 1 driven) and attack is the pick (0 a hammer-on or pull-off … 1 a hard pick); a chord part keeps the preset's own playing, except on electric_guitar:fingerstyle (a jazz archtop played with the fingers), whose chords and arpeggios play the model too. SOLO: "solo" (or solo: true on the map) plays the part as a soloist — vibrato grows into its sustained notes after the attack, a sustained note before a rest dies away instead of stopping, it breathes in its rests; render_score does this by itself for the ONE melodic line sounding while it plays (solo: false stops it; solo: {vibrato?, vibrato_rate? 0–1, delay?, min_note?, tail? seconds, share? 0–10, lane_below? s, irregular? 0–2} tunes it). Receipt: articulation {model, played_by, marked, styles, described?, solo?: {by, played, vibrato, tails}}.

controllers.description: With notes: the part's OWN continuous controllers, as a DAW lane — written into its MIDI as given, each value held until the next. cc: {"<controller 1–119>": [[beat, value 0–127], …]} in beat order (the mod wheel "1", expression "11", "74" …; not 6, 32, 38, 96–101); pitch_bend: [[beat, semitones −48…48], …] (the wheel, its range declared in the MIDI). A moving CC11 — CC1 on a wind, brass, string or bass part — is the part's written level through its notes (a swell on a held note) and colours its tone; the pitch wheel bends the notes. ≤ 16 controllers, ≤ 8192 points each.

name.description: Optional: a name for this job's files, e.g. "rainy-loop-3". Every file it returns downloads as <name>_<part>.<ext> (rainy-loop-3_Celesta.wav, rainy-loop-3_rough-mix.wav; one take: rainy-loop-3.wav), so the user can find them. Give each job its own name (a second take: "rainy-loop-3b"). Default: doseedo-<last 6 characters of the job id>.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_train_instrument
tools.description: Make a CUSTOM INSTRUMENT in your own sound: upload 30 s–3 min of ONE instrument playing (your own player, a rare or folk instrument, a prepared/invented instrument, a vintage synth) and doseedo trains a private adapter (LoRA) on its serving instrument model in about 1–2 minutes. After that, doseedo_render_midi {instrument: <the same instrument>, lora_id} plays ANY notes you write in that sound. Several takes help (up to 8 files; the first 3 min are used, ≥8 s required); a clean, solo, dry recording works best. instrument = the closest catalog instrument — it picks the model voice the adapter trains on (a shamisen trains as acoustic_guitar, a whistle as flute: doseedo_instruments lists each one's call.instrument). The notes are transcribed for you (pass notes to skip that). 20 credits. Result: lora_id, name, the windows it trained on, loss first→last, and `use` (the render args). Earlier ones: doseedo_list_jobs {kind:"train_instrument"}. Owner-only: no one else can render with it. Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (~1–2 min). Cancel: the plane has no stop for a running training — it runs to completion (credits spent), the job ends as canceled and its output is discarded. Only a job still queued at the plane is refunded by the plane's own failure refund.

audio_key.description: R2 ingest key of an uploaded audio file (from doseedo_get_upload_url / POST /api/upload/r2/ingest-url; starts with "ingest/"). One recording; or audio_keys for several.

audio_keys.description: Several uploaded takes of the SAME instrument (≤8).

audio_url.description: https URL of a recording (a doseedo result link — a separated stem works — or any public URL). Alternative to audio_key.

audio_urls.description: Several recording URLs of the same instrument (≤8).

instrument.description: REQUIRED. The catalog instrument it is closest to (call.instrument from doseedo_instruments, e.g. "violin", "acoustic_guitar", "flute", "percussion").

name.description: A name for it, e.g. "Grandpa's banjo" (≤80 chars).

notes.description: Optional: the notes played, one list per file — [[{pitch, start, end, velocity?}…]] in SECONDS. Omitted, they are transcribed.

drum_mode.description: true for an unpitched percussion recording.

steps.description: Training steps 50–800. Default 300 for ≤60 s of audio, 400 above.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_render_score
tools.description: Plays a whole arrangement you wrote in one call — film scoring, orchestral arrangement, background music, a song or instrumental (a film cue, a string quartet, a big-band chart): each part played by its doseedo instrument, one stem per part from bar 1 at your tempo, plus a summed mix. Input ONE of: parts[] ({name, instrument, timbre_preset?, lora_id?, players?, notes[]} — doseedo_instruments calls), midi_url (multi-track SMF), or musicxml_url (notation played as marked, at concert pitch). A file's parts are matched by name, then GM program; name any part with instruments {"<part name or index>": {instrument, timbre_preset?, players?}}. A chord on a one-line instrument is split into voices (one stem each). ★ SECTIONS: an instrument is ONE player; give a part players: N (2–8) and its line is played by N different players, summed into ONE section stem — an orchestra = violins I / II, violas, cellos, basses as five parts with players 6 / 6 / 4 / 4 / 3, horns 2–4 in unison; a choir = S/A/T/B parts on "choir" (an opera SATB chorus, or a consenting singer: parts[].timbre_audio_url), which SINGS parts[].lyrics ("Ooh" without), players 4–8 (recipe "choir"); a solo: no players. The WHOLE orchestra in one call: ≤ 32 lines and ≤ 96 player rows (players: N = N rows), any instruments together, ≤ 600 s. Drums: the drum model is a real kit, drum_engine "oneshot" a drum machine. Synths: synth_role + synth_genre. Timing: bpm and/or tempo_map ([{beat, bpm}]; doseedo_tempo_map lands film hits on downbeats). Result: parts[{name, instrument, url, fit, timbre, lora, players}] — fit.verdict / coverage = did it PLAY its notes (a failed part is re-rolled once; fit.rolls.missed = a roll not played as one), lora.applied = its adapter played — plus mix_url. Next: doseedo_mix {from_job}, then doseedo_session_from_stems {from_job, mix_job}. Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (~1–4 min). Cancel: a render that has not reached the GPU yet is stopped and its credits refunded; one already rendering finishes on the GPU (its credits are spent), the job ends as canceled and the output is discarded.

parts.description: The parts you wrote: [{name?, instrument, timbre_preset?, lora_id?, players?, lyrics?, notes:[{pitch, start_beats, duration_beats, velocity?, lyric?}], dynamics?}] — beats from bar 1, concert pitch. lyrics / lyric: a choir part's words. instrument/timbre_preset = a doseedo_instruments call. players = how many play the line: 1 (default) a soloist, 2–8 a SECTION (e.g. Violins I players 6).

tune.description: false = this part exactly as rendered (no light intonation pass; default true).

drum_engine.description: A drum / percussion part: "model" (default) = the drum model — a drummer playing the kit in a room (cymbals ring, hits vary, ghost notes speak): the sound for any acoustic kit, rock to jazz to a film cue. A take may drop or add a hit (parts[].fit.voices: missing / extra): render the part again for another take. "oneshot" = a one-shot kit generated for drum_genre, one sample per drum: every written hit lands exactly as written (a half-time bar stays half-time, a stop-time hit stays a hit), but it sounds programmed — the kit for electronic / drum-machine genres only (house, trap, 808). An acoustic kit (drum_kit: rock, punk, jazz, soul, a band seen playing) stays on the model, never oneshot — and a kit whose drum_genre is real drums (funk, boom bap, lo-fi, breakbeat: a sampled break is a drummer; its dust comes from the mix, doseedo_mix style "1990s-hiphop" / "lofi-hiphop") plays on drum_kit whatever is asked (warnings say so). A take that drops a hit is rendered again. Its pads (GM): kick 35/36, snare 38/40, rim 37, clap 39, hats 42/44/46, toms 41–50, crash 49/57, ride 51/59, tambourine 54, cowbell 56, bongos 60/61, congas 62–64, shaker 69/70/82, guiro 73/74, claves 75, woodblock 76/77, triangle 80/81. "break" = a chopped BREAK, the way jungle and drum and bass make their drums: an acoustic break from the break library, sped up to the piece and sliced — by break_plan, or with no plan by the part's own drum notes (each note plays the slice that starts with that drum). A kit part only.

break_plan.description: With drum_engine "break": the chops — {figure?: "amen", events: [[at, src, len, gain?, flags?, rate?], …]}: `len` sixteenths of the break from its step `src` (0–127) laid at sixteenth `at` of the piece (fractions allowed); flags 1 = reversed, 2 = far (heard through a high-pass); rate = an extra pitch-up. A band generator writes it; omit it to have the part's own drum notes pick the slices.

drum_genre.description: With drum_engine "oneshot": the kit's genre / words, e.g. "house", "techno", "trap", "synthwave": a dry drum-machine kit. A real-drums genre ("boom bap", "lo-fi", "breakbeat", "funk") puts the part on the drum model's drum_kit. Default: the instrument.

synth_role.description: A part on instrument "synth": the patch made for it — "808" (a sub that follows the kick), "bass", "pad", "lead", "pluck". The patch plays every note exactly as written, beside the band. Without synth_role / synth_genre / synth_words the synth model plays the part.

synth_genre.description: With instrument "synth": the genre the patch is made for — "trap", "house", "techno", "synthwave", "lo-fi", "dnb"… or free words; "tech" = a computed voice (a gliding sine sub, a dark pluck, a filtered pad), exactly in tune.

synth_words.description: With instrument "synth": a few words that turn the patch ("dark", "bright", "warm", "detuned", "short").

synth_patch.description: With instrument "synth": a SAMPLED patch in place of the computed voice — "<pack>:<patch id or name>" ("xv5080:PR-C/056") or a pitched pack ("bass808"). See render_midi synth_patch.

synth_engine.description: A synth part: "oneshot" = the patch (the default once synth_role / synth_genre / synth_words is given), "model" = the synth model.

synth_fx.description: A synth part's own processing, as an analog voice has it: {sub_db?: -24..0 (the same patch an octave below, in the middle, dB under the part), widen?: 0..1 (the part above ~180 Hz spread left / right; the low end stays in the middle and the spread cancels in mono), filter?: {res?: 0..1, sweep: [[beat, Hz], …]} (a resonant low-pass whose cutoff moves through the points, log between them — a slow sweep across the form builds a song)}. A band generator writes it for an analog bassline, its sweep following the piece's build. The receipt's synth_engine.fx says what was done.

vaefix.description: false = this part's decode exactly as rendered (no VAE spectral corrector; default true).

dynamics_curve.description: What colours this part's TONE over time: auto (default) = its dynamics lane when that moves, else its note velocities when they vary — soft darker, loud brighter, on every instrument but drums; off = one colour throughout; velocity = the velocities even with a lane; cc11/cc1 = that MIDI CC lane (a midi_url part). Receipt: parts[].dynamics.

level_cut.description: This part's level UNDER its written level over time: rows [beat, dB from -24 to 0, velocity steps], each in force until the next. The dB comes off the rendered stem as gain on every instrument (a kit and a strummed or played part too, whose velocities are their touch); the steps say how many velocity steps were ALSO taken off the notes there, so the level law reads them as written and the cut counts once (0 when the notes are as written). A band generator with dynamics_depth "records" writes it; a mix {from_job} reads it.

dynamics.description: The part's written LEVEL over time, as a DAW automation lane: [{beat, velocity 1–127}] in beat order, linear between points, a step = two points on one beat, held after the last (p 52, mf 80, f 96, ff 112). A velocity says how a note STARTS; this says how it goes on — a crescendo on a held note: [{beat: 0, velocity: 52}, {beat: 8, velocity: 96}]. Its tone follows it, through a held note too, and doseedo_mix {from_job} rides the level to it. A MusicXML score's dynamics + hairpins arrive as this lane on their own.

players.description: How many players play this line: 1 (default) = a soloist (a single line on a Section row — ensemble_strings / ensemble_brass / ensemble_winds — is its section_players); 2–8 = a SECTION — the line played by that many different players (each its own recording and performance), summed into ONE section stem. A string section = violins I, violins II, violas, cellos, basses with players 4–8 each; a choir section = singers (Soprano players 6 = six sopranos). Each player renders (and costs) like a part.

timbre_audio_url.description: This part's OWN timbre: a recording of the singer (a choir part) or sound it should take on (a drum part too: a kit, a ride or a snare recording on the drum model — not drum_engine "oneshot" or a sampled instrument, which play their own samples) — an https URL, or the audio_key doseedo_get_upload_url returned for a file on your machine. The first 30 s are used; a clean solo take of the voice, 10–30 s, works best. Wins over the preset's voice; a choir part keeps the choir's adapter and sings in THIS voice. receipt: parts[].timbre. A VOICE only with consent: the user's own, or a singer who agreed to it (doseedo's Terms) — never to imitate a real artist or anyone else without their permission.

timbre_audio_urls.description: Several recordings (≤ 6): a section's players (players: N) and a split chord's voices take them in turn — a choir section of several singers of your own. A VOICE only with consent: the user's own, or a singer who agreed to it (doseedo's Terms) — never to imitate a real artist or anyone else without their permission.

articulation.description: HOW the part is played, a passage at a time — no per-note work needed: a style for the whole part ("legato"), passages [{from, to, style?, dynamics?}] (beats from bar 1, [from, to)), or {style?, passages?, notes?: [{at, pitch?, style?, vibrato?, hairpin?, curve?, bend?}], curve?: [[beat, dB], …], unit?: "beats"|"seconds"}. Styles: legato tenuto portato staccato staccatissimo spiccato accent marcato sfz fp swell crescendo decrescendo espressivo molto_vibrato senza_vibrato breathy growl bright dark fall doit scoop gliss (aliases: slur, short, >, ^, sf, cresc, dim, subtone, glissando…; a list combines them). A sentence where a name goes ("short, warm, no vibrato") is read for its lengths, vibrato and tone only (receipt described); an accent, a hairpin or a bend is named on its passage or note. dynamics: "mf", or a hairpin over the span "p<f", "f>p", "p<f>p" (ppp…fff). curve = a RELATIVE level curve (±18 dB) added to every note under it: a master / section swell over existing dynamics. Any span or note may also set vibrato, vibrato_rate, bright, breath, rough (0–1) and attack ("slur" | "tongue" | 0–1); a note: hairpin "<" ">" "<>", curve (its level 0–127 through it), bend (semitones through it). Later passages / notes win field by field; curves add. On an instrument with an articulation model (doseedo_instruments articulation) the part plays on that model (vibrato, colour, attacks, in-note shapes); elsewhere lengths, accents, dynamics, curves and bends still apply. On a GUITAR (electric, or a steel-string acoustic) a LINE (a lead, a riff, a fill: one note at a time) plays on its model: bright is the drive (0 clean, straight into the board … 1 driven) and attack is the pick (0 a hammer-on or pull-off … 1 a hard pick); a chord part keeps the preset's own playing, except on electric_guitar:fingerstyle (a jazz archtop played with the fingers), whose chords and arpeggios play the model too. SOLO: "solo" (or solo: true on the map) plays the part as a soloist — vibrato grows into its sustained notes after the attack, a sustained note before a rest dies away instead of stopping, it breathes in its rests; render_score does this by itself for the ONE melodic line sounding while it plays (solo: false stops it; solo: {vibrato?, vibrato_rate? 0–1, delay?, min_note?, tail? seconds, share? 0–10, lane_below? s, irregular? 0–2} tunes it). Receipt: articulation {model, played_by, marked, styles, described?, solo?: {by, played, vibrato, tails}}.

vocoder.description: A SUNG part (instrument "voice") spoken through a synth — what a band generator's vocoder or talkbox chair carries: its top line is sung (one voice, its lyrics), and every note of the part (a chord's too) is played by the style's synth through that take. ensemble (a polysynth and string machine singing the chords) | strings (the 1980 string-machine vocoder: ten bands, wide, its held vowels sweeping up) | robot | house | choir | talkbox | talkbox_house. receipt: parts[].vocoder.

lyrics.description: A SUNG part (instrument "choir"): the words it sings, ONE SYLLABLE PER NOTE in time order, a new line per sung phrase — a chord's notes share an onset, so every voice sings that syllable. Hyphens split a word's syllables ("Glo-ri-a in ex-cel-sis De-o"), "_" alone holds the previous syllable over the next note (a melisma), one word ("Ah", "Mm") is sung on every note. Omit = "Ooh" on every note. notes[].lyric places syllables one by one instead (it wins). Other instruments ignore it.

lyric.description: A sung part: the syllable this note sings ("glo-" = more of the word follows, "a", "_" = hold the previous syllable).

generator.description: Alternative to parts: a BAND GENERATOR plays the piece — no notes written by you. Its id ("jazz") or {id, seed?, bars? | seconds?, key?, lead?, band?, theme?, changes?, song?, only?, layers?, dynamics?, hits?, lay_out?, thin?, texture?, articulation?, builds?, ending?, intro?, first_bar_at_seconds?, swing?, solo_swing?, pedal?, rubato?}: the generator writes every part (drums, bass, piano and a lead for jazz — lead: "none" = the rhythm section alone, a bed under dialogue; "scat" = sung) in its genre, with its own form and changes, at this call's bpm / tempo_map; length = bars, or seconds, or duration_seconds. DIRECT it in seconds from the piece's start (turned into beats on your tempo_map) or in beats: dynamics [{at_seconds, level: none|low|medium|high|peak, ramp?}] — the band follows it bar by bar; ramp: true = the level is REACHED there, moving evenly from the mark before (a crescendo, a falling away); hits [{at_seconds, kind?: light|medium|full}] — the band lands that moment together (a cut, a punchline): full = everyone with a crash, medium = the rhythm section, light = one stroke; who = only those parts land it, stroke = the one drum of the kit that sounds (kick, snare, rim, clap, hat, open hat, crash, tom, high tom, floor tom); lay_out [{from_seconds?, to_seconds?, who?, only?}] — who RESTS where: no name = the lead (dialogue) while the rhythm section plays on; who = the parts that rest (a part's name, a family — strings, brass, winds, keys, percussion — "rhythm", "lead", "all" for a silence — a hit on its first beat is the stop chord, choked, and nothing else sounds inside a rest asked); only = the parts that play on while everyone else rests; no from_seconds = from the start (a part ENTERING at to_seconds), no to_seconds = to the end (a part LEAVING); thin [{from_seconds?, to_seconds?, to?: beats|halves|bars, who?}] — who plays THINNER there (under a voice, a low stretch): the named parts, or everyone but the tune, keep only what they play on the beat, on the bar's two halves, or on the bar line; texture [{from_seconds?, to_seconds?, who, plays? | level?, value?}] — WHAT a part plays there (whole bars), always the style's own writing for that part: plays held (a pad) | pedal (a drone) | pulse | arpeggio | ostinato | walk | stabs | comp | line | run (the scale rushed up into each next bar's chord, value = its notes, sixteenths by default), a drum part four_on_the_floor | backbeat | half_time | ride | light | full, value eighths | sixteenths … for an even one; the part's bars are replaced by bars the style wrote for it over the same chords (these bars at another level, or another stretch of the piece) that ARE that texture; level instead of plays = the part as the style plays it at that level while the band stays where it is. A texture the style does not play on that part is not applied — the answer's direction.texture says what the part can play (doseedo_generators {direction: {textures: true}} lists it up front); articulation [{from_seconds?, to_seconds?, who, style}] — HOW the named parts are played over that stretch: style legato | staccato | marcato | accent | spiccato | tenuto | portato | espressivo | senza_vibrato … (a part's articulation styles; a list is several), laid on those parts as a passage — no note changes; neither time = the whole piece. Pizzicato, tremolo, harmonics and mutes are another SOUND: that stretch is played on a sibling stem in it (a seated player of that instrument whose name or timbre_preset says it, else the catalog's own pizz / muted instrument, made a part) and direction.sound says which — or what to seat; builds [{into_seconds, beats?, drop?, roll?}] — a build into a moment: everyone swells and the drums roll over the beats before it (one bar by default) — only a drum the style itself plays (a bed with none swells); roll: "none" | a part's name says who rolls; drop: true = the bass and bass drum leave the last beat empty, "all" = everyone does where a riser sounds into it. Risers, cinematic hits and braams seated in band sound on the builds and hits in any style (fx_seats in the answer); ending {kind: cut|button|ring|fade|form, at_seconds?, chord?} — cut = nothing sounds from there on (a hard out), button = one short hit and nothing after, ring = a last chord held to the end, fade = the band falls away into a soft held chord, form = no ending (full level to the last beat); nothing sounds past the piece, a ring or fade asked too late to ring moves back to the bar line that leaves it room (moved_from_beats), and over the caller's changes the last chord is the caller's own tonic chord (a Cmaj7 loop ends on Cmaj7, its root in the bass; a last chord already there is left as voiced) unless chord says "as written" or names one; a player asked in for the end plays that chord — ending.chord in the answer names what sounds; left out, the piece ends the way its style's records do (a ring-out or a fade over its last few seconds, direction.ending.default: true) — on a tempo_map it ends as its form does; intro: false — it starts on the tune; first_bar_at_seconds — the piece begins MID-BAR, its first bar line that far in (a fixed doseedo_tempo_map's music_offset_s: its bar lines are then where the map landed your hits, and the piece still starts on the cue's first frame). A hit with cut: true is a picture cut to MARK: struck on the beat the cut falls on, left out where it falls between beats. YOUR OWN BAND: band [{instrument, timbre_preset?, name?, chair?: drums|bass|comp|lead|extra, players?, timbre_audio_url?}] — who is seated, in place of the generator's own players, each as a part takes it (doseedo_instruments): the style is written for THESE instruments and each comes back called exactly so; timbre_audio_url = that player's own SOUND, a recording whose tone it takes on as a part's timbre_audio_url does (a brighter or darker recording moves the take's tone the same way), matched to the part by the player's name. A player the style has no chair for is a guest (guests in the answer): it plays only what you give it — the theme, where a statement names it. YOUR OWN MUSIC, arranged by the generator (a score's theme and chords): theme {notes: [[pitch, beat, beats, velocity], …], statements?, also?} — the tune, beats from its first bar line; the generator's own tune comes out and yours goes in, every note as written. With no statements it is said wherever the generator's tune was, on whoever had it; statements [{at_seconds, on?, from_beat?, beats?, octave?, transpose?, stretch?, name?}] say where and by whom (on = part names as lay_out takes them; from_beat / beats = a part of it — its head, a fragment; octave; transpose in semitones; stretch 2 = notes twice as long; name = another tune from also {name: notes}; mode: major | minor = that statement in the PARALLEL mode of the theme's tonic — its third, sixth and seventh moved, nothing else; harmony [{on, at}] = parts that play the statement WITH its carrier, in its rhythm, at third_below | third_above | sixth_below | sixth_above | octave_below | octave_above — in the key, on a chord tone where a note is long or on a strong beat, never a second from the tune and never across it). changes "Dm | Bb | Gm | A" — your chords, one cell a bar ("Dm G7" = two in a bar), as a loop, or [{at_seconds, changes}]; played bar after bar as given, so a statement placed on the loop's first bar is over its first chord. A theme with no changes is HARMONISED (the chords go to the tune; the tune is never changed), in key or the key the tune is in. FEEL (swung styles; left out, each piece and soloist draws its own as records do): swing light|medium|hard — the band's eighths; solo_swing straight|light|medium|hard — the soloist's ("straight" = even eighths laid back over the swing). STYLE TRANSFER — song: {melody: [[pitch, beat, beats], …], changes: "C | Am | F | G7" (one cell a bar, the WHOLE song), sections: [{label, bars, energy?}], meter?, bpm?, key?, phrasing?, answers?: [[pitch, beat, beats], …] (the band's answers to the tune, in its rests: a chair of the genre plays them), answer_by?, lines?: [[pitch, beat, beats], …] (the song's own instrumental figures — a riff, two voices in thirds: a colour of the genre plays them where the song does, its rhythm section playing the genre), line_by?} plays YOUR SONG in this genre and keeps it exactly: its length, its sections, its chart bar for bar and every note of its tune from bar one (every pitch, in order, sung in the genre's phrasing: an eighth early where the genre pushes the beat or its band pushes the change, its eighths swung in a swing; phrasing: "as written" keeps every onset exactly); the generator decides only how its chairs play it (lead: "none" = the genre's rhythm section without the tune; "backing" = its whole backing, every chair but the tune's, for a singer). A melody alone is harmonised; chords alone get the genre's own tune; parts: [{name, notes}] (a MIDI arrangement) is read for its tune and chart. A genre in another metre (a waltz, 6/8, 12/8) plays the song re-metered by the meter-change rule and says what moved. only: "bass" | ["bass", "drums"] returns just those parts — the genre's line for one stem, written with the whole band. SEVERAL STYLES, ONE PIECE — layers: [{id, only?, band?, lead?, seed?}] (1–3): other band generators play THIS piece with it, each as a song in its own style (the same bars, sections, chords and tempo) and each giving its own parts: an 80s synth band with a process piece's mallets and clarinets and a meditation's drone is {id: "synthwave", layers: [{id: "minimalism", only: ["Mallets", "winds"]}, {id: "meditation", only: "Drone"}]}. only = the parts or a family it gives (left out: all but its drums and bass, the host keeping the floor); lead = the instrument that carries the tune in that style ("flute", "bansuri"; the host's lead leaves). Names two styles share come back apart ("Pad (ambient)"); a lay_out / thin / texture / articulation / hit that names parts goes to the style that has them, a family or "all" to every style. The same seed is the same piece: doseedo_generators {generator, …} shows it (free) before you render. Result: parts as for any score (a player the piece gave no note has no part), plus generator {id, seed, bars, key, form, changes, direction: what was applied, row by row — a row it could not play says applied: false or not_applied with why, a hit some players could not land not_landed, a row that sounded nothing sounded: false —, guests: the players it seated with no chair, silent: every seated player who played nothing and why, song: what was kept} — on the submit reply (prepared.generator) and on the finished job's output alike.

lyrics.description: The words the generator's SUNG chair sings (a voice lead, a vocoder, a talkbox), a line a phrase: laid on its tune phrase by phrase, each line in turn. Omit = the style's own words.

dynamics_depth.description: How deep the dynamics go. "records" (the default) = each instrument as far as its level moves inside the genre's records (a kit a little, guitars more, strings and horns most) — your `dynamics` marks at that depth, or with none the piece's own form, each section under its loudest. "written" = every chair takes one touch and a form plays at the level its writers wrote.

blueprint.description: Play the piece in the SHAPE OF ONE REAL RECORD of the generator's genre: "draw" = a record drawn on the seed (two seeds, two records), or a record id from an earlier answer. Its tempo and length where you set none, its sections' levels laid over the generator's form by role (its loudest section on the form's loudest), its builds, where it thins, and its ending. Your own bpm / bars / seconds / dynamics / ending win (your dynamics marks replace its whole section shape). The answer's generator.blueprint names the record and what was and was not applied. Left out = a drawn record's shape at the piece's own length — except a song, layers, or a piece on a picture's clock (tempo_map, hits, a first bar placed), which keep their own; false = the generator's own shape.

pedal.description: The PIANO's damper pedal: off | light | harmony (the foot changes with each chord: every chord rings into the next) | bar, or a depth 0-1. Left out = the style's own.

rubato.description: A generator whose style BREATHES (film_noir: the first bar laid out, each section closing broader, the end slowing into its last chord) plays its own tempo map unless you hold the clock (your tempo_map, hits, first_bar_at_seconds/beats, a song). false = one tempo. The answer's $generator.rubato says whether it played.

score_key.description: Alternative to parts: a score file on YOUR machine — doseedo_get_upload_url {filename: "cue.mid" | "cue.musicxml" | "cue.mscz"} → PUT the file → its score_key (kept 24 h). A big score sent as a file, not as notes in this call.

score_url.description: Alternative to parts: a score file URL — MIDI, MusicXML or a MuseScore .mscz / .mscx, told apart by its content.

midi_url.description: Alternative to parts: a multi-track Standard MIDI File (≤ 2 MiB) — a doseedo result link or a public https URL. Channel 10 = drums: the kit, or the one percussion instrument a part is named for (Bass Drum, Cymbals, Bass Drum & Cymbals, Triangle…). A track's CC11 lane (CC1 on a wind / brass / string / bass part) is its written dynamics: a held note swells as it says.

musicxml_url.description: Alternative to parts: a MusicXML score (.musicxml / .xml / .mxl, ≤ 8 MiB) exported from Dorico, Sibelius, Finale, MuseScore, or written by you — or a MuseScore file itself (.mscz / .mscx), read with all its markings.

instruments.description: Name the instrument for any part: {"Violin I": {"instrument": "violin", "players": 6}, "2": {"instrument": "acoustic_guitar", "timbre_preset": "koto:preset1"}, "Choir": {"instrument": "choir", "players": 6, "lyrics": "Glo-ri-a"}} — key = the part name or its 0-based index; players makes a MIDI / MusicXML part a section, lyrics gives a sung part its words (as parts[].lyrics), timbre_audio_url / timbre_audio_urls its own singer (with their consent, as parts[] says) or sound (as parts[]: {"Soprano": {"timbre_audio_url": "https://…/singer.wav"}}), drum_engine "oneshot" (+ drum_genre) plays a file's drum part on a one-shot kit ({"Drums": {"drum_engine": "oneshot"}} — no instrument keeps the part's own). Wins over the name/program match.

bpm.description: Tempo of the parts (10–400). Required with parts[] unless tempo_map is given; on a file it sets the speed and keeps the score's fermatas / rit. / tempo changes.

tempo_map.description: Tempo changes [{beat, bpm}] (first point at beat 0). Overrides a file's own tempo.

duration_seconds.description: Render length (default: the last note + 2 s; ≤ 600).

mix.description: Ignored: every render bounces a summed mix of its parts (mix_url) — on a free plan the mix is what the render hands back.

tune.description: Light intonation on every winds / brass / strings part (default true): held, clearly pitched notes the model rendered 15–85 cents off are moved toward their written pitch, to a small natural residual — attacks, vibrato and fast notes as played. Receipt: parts[].tune. false = every part as rendered (or parts[].tune false for one).

band_decode.description: ON by default (false = the plain decode): every part whose instrument the band decoder table gives a model (guitars, acoustic and electric piano, cello, arco double bass) has its takes' 1–7 kHz rebuilt by that model (see doseedo_render_midi band_decode) — a band generator's parts included; every other part (drums, bass, horns, winds) is left as rendered. A score with no such part is left as rendered; a guitar part played on tape at a speed with no band model (tape −12: a bossa's nylon) keeps its plain decode — receipt band_decode {applied, decodes, ms, why_not, tape_plain}.

dsp_doubles.description: How a SECTION's players 2..N are made (parts[].players). Default: shared for a LARGE ORCHESTRA (2+ string / brass / wind / choir sections of 3+ players, 10+ players in them), off for anything smaller (off = each player its own GPU render). shared = where every player of a section would hear ONE recording (a high passage on tape, an adapter's own reference, one recording of yours), players 2..N are made from player 1 on the CPU — its notes, its own intonation, timing and tone — instead of a render each; two parts of one instrument in unison stop being one take twice. all = every section that way (fastest; players with recordings of their own lose their spread). Receipt: parts[].players.dsp_doubles.

vaefix.description: VAE spectral corrector on every winds / brass / strings part (default true): the decoder's low-mid fog under each instrument's register is trimmed, mic hiss removed only where present. Receipt: parts[].vaefix. false = every decode as rendered (or parts[].vaefix false for one).

seed.description: Random seed (reuse to re-render close to the same performance).

articulation.description: The SCORE-WIDE articulation layer, under every part's own (parts[].articulation / instruments rows, applied after it): a master curve or a tutti passage legato for all. Same shape as parts[].articulation: HOW the part is played, a passage at a time — no per-note work needed: a style for the whole part ("legato"), passages [{from, to, style?, dynamics?}] (beats from bar 1, [from, to)), or {style?, passages?, notes?: [{at, pitch?, style?, vibrato?, hairpin?, curve?, bend?}], curve?: [[beat, dB], …], unit?: "beats"|"seconds"}. Styles: legato tenuto portato staccato staccatissimo spiccato accent marcato sfz fp swell crescendo decrescendo espressivo molto_vibrato senza_vibrato breathy growl bright dark fall doit scoop gliss (aliases: slur, short, >, ^, sf, cresc, dim, subtone, glissando…; a list combines them). A sentence where a name goes ("short, warm, no vibrato") is read for its lengths, vibrato and tone only (receipt described); an accent, a hairpin or a bend is named on its passage or note. dynamics: "mf", or a hairpin over the span "p<f", "f>p", "p<f>p" (ppp…fff). curve = a RELATIVE level curve (±18 dB) added to every note under it: a master / section swell over existing dynamics. Any span or note may also set vibrato, vibrato_rate, bright, breath, rough (0–1) and attack ("slur" | "tongue" | 0–1); a note: hairpin "<" ">" "<>", curve (its level 0–127 through it), bend (semitones through it). Later passages / notes win field by field; curves add. On an instrument with an articulation model (doseedo_instruments articulation) the part plays on that model (vibrato, colour, attacks, in-note shapes); elsewhere lengths, accents, dynamics, curves and bends still apply. On a GUITAR (electric, or a steel-string acoustic) a LINE (a lead, a riff, a fill: one note at a time) plays on its model: bright is the drive (0 clean, straight into the board … 1 driven) and attack is the pick (0 a hammer-on or pull-off … 1 a hard pick); a chord part keeps the preset's own playing, except on electric_guitar:fingerstyle (a jazz archtop played with the fingers), whose chords and arpeggios play the model too. SOLO: "solo" (or solo: true on the map) plays the part as a soloist — vibrato grows into its sustained notes after the attack, a sustained note before a rest dies away instead of stopping, it breathes in its rests; render_score does this by itself for the ONE melodic line sounding while it plays (solo: false stops it; solo: {vibrato?, vibrato_rate? 0–1, delay?, min_note?, tail? seconds, share? 0–10, lane_below? s, irregular? 0–2} tunes it). Receipt: articulation {model, played_by, marked, styles, described?, solo?: {by, played, vibrato, tails}}.

name.description: Optional: a name for this job's files, e.g. "rainy-loop-3". Every file it returns downloads as <name>_<part>.<ext> (rainy-loop-3_Celesta.wav, rainy-loop-3_rough-mix.wav; one take: rainy-loop-3.wav), so the user can find them. Give each job its own name (a second take: "rainy-loop-3b"). Default: doseedo-<last 6 characters of the job id>.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_mix
tools.description: MIXING and MASTERING: each part levelled, panned, high-passed, given its depth on a shared reverb, mastered to a loudness target — a WAV AND `mixgraph`, the mix as a document. After doseedo_render_score pass from_job (its parts and the instruments they play are the stems); or stems: [{name, audio_url, instrument?}]. An orchestra (strings / winds / brass / timpani / harp…) is SEATED by default (film-orchestral: violins left, low strings right, brass behind, each seat at its depth in a 2.3 s hall, written dynamics riding the faders); others mixed blind. style: an id or words — the style parameter lists every id (scoring halls, jazz-combo, big-band, brass and marching bands, soul, rock-band and the other guitar bands, blues, country, reggae, disco, the decades). guitar_tone = guitar sound. balance {part: dB} moves parts on top of the levelling (+3 = a melody forward). Change the mix: edit the returned mixgraph — strips[] {stem, gain_db, pan, seat, chain, sends}, buses[] (verb = the hall; a section's fader_db = its level), master.chain, automation [{target: "strips.<stem>.gain_db", points: [[seconds, dB]…]}] for rides (dB off the strip's gain_db: 0 = as set, -60 mutes) — and call again with mix_job (this job_id) + only your edits (or the whole mixgraph + the same stems): rendered as written, rails reported, no credits. Then doseedo_session_from_stems {from_job, mix_job: <this job_id>} → the DAW project at this mix's levels and pans. TO PICTURE: dialogue (the VO; the music ducks under it), music_offset_s (bar 1 on the picture), length_s (cut + end fade). Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (~15–90 s). Cancel: the plane has no stop for a running mix — it runs to completion (credits spent), the job ends as canceled and its output is discarded. Only a job still queued at the plane is refunded by the plane's own failure refund.

from_job.description: MCP: a doseedo_render_score job_id — its parts are the stems, each with the instrument it plays, and each part's written dynamics (its mean velocity) set its balance. A render made from a BAND GENERATOR (render_score {generator}) is mixed in the style that generator names for its genre — a dub in its spring tank and tape echo, surf guitars in a spring, a fifties slapback — at the tempo it plays, unless you pass style.

from_jobs.description: MCP: ONE cue rendered as several doseedo_render_score jobs (its parts split across renders): every job's parts are the stems, balanced and ridden by their written dynamics as one score.

without.description: MCP, with from_job / from_jobs: the parts LEFT OUT of this mix, by name (a section's name leaves out its players) — the same render mixed again without them: nothing is played again, every other part keeps its take.

with_stems.description: With from_job / from_jobs: stems that play BESIDE the render's own parts — a part of the same cue that another job rendered (a drum machine's or a synth's own doseedo_render_midi take): [{name, audio_url, instrument?}]. The render's parts are read from its job (on a free plan too, which is handed no part links); these are mixed with them.

stems.description: [{name, audio_url, instrument?}] — the stems (≤ 32). instrument = the sound it plays (a doseedo_instruments id: "violin", "timpani", "harp"), which decides how it is mixed; without it the name decides.

mixgraph.description: An edited mix — the mixgraph a doseedo_mix returned, changed — rendered against the same stems (from_job or stems). With mix_job: ONLY what you change (strips[] by stem, automation[] rides by target — points: [] removes one, buses[] by id, master) — the rest is that mix as stored. A mixgraph marked `partial` (its rides summarized) is refused without mix_job. Omit for a fresh mix.

mix_job.description: MCP: a doseedo_mix job_id to edit — its whole stored mix (every ride) is the base, mixgraph is applied on top, and its stems are reused when you pass no from_job / stems.

style.description: A mix style: an id or words ("dry 90s rock"). guitar_tone.description: The guitars' and bass guitar's own SOUND. Every guitar and bass-guitar part (an upright played pizzicato too; never a synth bass or an 808) gets a tone by default ("auto"): a mixing chain for the style — compression, the amp's voicing and speaker, chorus / phaser / tremolo, its own echo and reverb, in stereo — fitted to that stem (drive only where the genre is driven, and less on a take that already came out amped; an acoustic gets EQ, compression and a room, never an amp; a bass stays centred and dry). "none" = as rendered (dry, mono). Or name one: a tone id, or words ("surf", "dark trap loop", "80s chorus") — for every guitar, or {part name: tone} for one.
