bpm.description: The music's tempo: a guitar tone's echoes (an eighth, a dotted eighth) land on it. from_job fills it.

vintage.description: A period medium over any style, after the mix: "tape" = 7.5 ips tape (saturation, wow and flutter, a low hiss); "shellac" = a 78 played back (mono, ~90 Hz–5.5 kHz with the reproducer's presence, a 1.3 Hz wow, surface noise that swishes once a turn, crackle). "none" takes a style's own medium off (golden-age-cartoon carries tape). Its node (master.chain type vintage: noise_db, crackle, hi_hz …) is editable in the returned mixgraph.

balance.description: {part name: dB in -12..12} — your balance on top of the levelling (and of the written dynamics a from_job reads).

dynamics.description: Fader rides from written dynamics: {part name: [[onset_seconds, velocity 0-127], …]}. from_job fills it from the score (pp to ff ≈ 17 dB); pass {} for no rides.

generator.description: The band generator the stems were rendered from (its id). The mix gives each of its parts the EQ its genre's records' mixes put on that part (the DSP plane's mix_eq table; a part it holds nothing for is mixed as before). from_job fills it.

generator_parts.description: The parts the generator played (part names): only these take its EQ — a stem from another job keeps its strip. from_job fills it; left out, every stem is the generator's.

tune_parts.description: The parts that carry the tune (part names): a seated mix (the scoring stages, the chamber and orchestral styles) seats them no lower than its band's own chairs, never as colour at the back of the stage, and from_job reads no written balance on them. from_job fills it with a band generator's lead chair.

dynamics_carried.description: {part name: top velocity} — parts whose stems already play their written level (a render part's dynamics_level receipt, up to its top_vel). Their rides count it: no doubled swing. from_job fills it.

dynamics_cut.description: {part name: [[seconds, dB ≤ 0], …]} — a level the part's stems already play UNDER their written dynamics (a band generator's form at the records' depth: a render part's level_cut). The mix leaves it in: its held-note level check does not take it back. from_job fills it.

moves_plan.description: The SPACE a band generator's style leaves, as the mix plays it: {risers: [{from_s, to_s, kind: "build" | "drop" | "breath" | "outro", shut?, every_s?}], dry: [[from_s, to_s]], blurbs: [seconds]} — a build's riser swells into the space, the rooms the rhythm section does not feed shut through it, a blurb answers the lead in its rests. Played only by a mix style with moves (lofi-soft-rock). from_job fills it from a generator that leaves space.

written_level.description: [[seconds, velocity], …] — the whole score's written level, the loudest part sounding, held until the next row (0 = nothing plays). The tonal match reads only the passages it writes loud (f and louder), so a pp passage keeps its darkness. from_job fills it.

levels.description: The level the music is MEANT to play at over time: [[seconds, "none" | "low" | "medium" | "high" | "peak"], …] in time order, each held until the next row (a third item true = that level is REACHED there, moving evenly from the row before). The mix measures its own sum, stretch by stretch, and holds each stretch to its level's place — peak the loudest, high 3.5 LU under it, medium 6, low 10 — so a thin passage is not lost under a full one and the band coming in is a step, not a jump. from_job fills it from a band generator's own dynamics; pass [] for none.

level_range_lu.description: How far apart "low" and "peak" sit, in LU (default 10; about 7 for music that plays under speech — the rungs between scale with it).

shapes.description: The director's dynamics keyframes on this music, seconds into it: [{curve, at_s, to_s?}, …] — curve "fadein" | "cresc" | "swell" | "steady" | "decresc" | "fadeout" (each over at_s..to_s, 4 s without one) or "accent" | "subito" | "stop" (at at_s). The mix measures its own sum over each and rides it only by what the music did not play: a crescendo it already plays is left alone; a stop the music played on through goes silent after its beat, to the next keyframe or for a breath. output.report.master.shape_follow says what it read and rode, keyframe by keyframe.

room.description: An orchestra's room: "studio" (intimate scoring stage, ~1.2 s, close), "stage" (~1.8 s), "hall" (the default scoring hall, ~2.3 s), "cathedral" (~4 s, wet) — or 0..1 between them. Sets the decay, size and how wet every seat sits.

dynamics_ride.description: How hard the written dynamics move the faders: 1 = default (pp to ff ≈ 17 dB), 0 = no rides, up to 1.5.

tonal_match.description: Nudge the master toward professionally mixed orchestral references (default on for the orchestral styles). Its presence and air are judged only where the score is written loud (written_level), so a pp passage keeps its darkness.

target_lufs.description: Master loudness, -24..-6 LUFS (default: the style's — -18 for film-orchestral, -14 for the blind default). Met within ~0.3 LU (a loud target clips the shortest transients first); output.loudness says what landed, and why when short. With mix_job it re-masters the stored mix. A delivery (doseedo_score_to_picture) lays a mix of fewer parts than its fullest cue under this, at its share (the mix names its parts): pick the loudness of the scene's full band, not of the part.

dialogue.description: The VO / dialogue on the picture's timeline (≤ 4): [{name?, audio_url}]. The music ducks under each line until the voice sits duck.vo_over_db over it, with a 1–4 kHz carve while it talks; the voice joins after the music's master chain. Report: output.dialogue.lines [{start_s, end_s, duck_db, vo_over_music_db}] as mixed.

duck.description: How the music sits under the dialogue: {vo_over_db (default 7 dB — a broadcast mix's 6–10), carve_db (default 3, at 1–4 kHz), max_db (default 12), include (default true; false = the music bed alone, ducked as if the voice played)}.

music_offset_s.description: Where bar 1 of the music sits on the picture (seconds, ≤ 600; the program ≤ 600 s): every music stem — and its rides — starts this late; the dialogue does not move.

length_s.description: The program's length (a :30 = 30; ≤ 600 s): the mix is cut there with end_fade_s (default 0.5 s); the room's tail never runs past it.

end_fade_s.description: With length_s: the fade at the program's end (0–10 s, default 0.5).

print_sections.description: Also print every section as its own stem: output.section_stems [{name, members, url}] — a 24-bit WAV per section (its players, their room and hall share, through the mix's own master), and the dialogue as one; the prints add up to the mix (report.prints.sum_error_db). Sections are the mix's group buses (film-orchestral-sections: strings / woodwinds / brass / percussion / keys_harp; parts in none print as "other"). About twice the render time; no extra credits. Works with mix_job too.

print_parts.description: Also print every PART alone as its own stem: output.part_stems [{name, url}] — a 24-bit WAV per part (that player, their room and hall share, through the mix's own master), all the mix's length and summing to the mix: the LAYERS a game fades in and out over a looping mix, or stems an editor mutes one by one. Instead of print_sections, not with it. About twice the render. Per-part stems come with Pro: a free plan is handed the mix.

loop.description: Make the mix a LOOP that repeats seamlessly: {bars, bpm, beats_per_bar?} (the loop is bars × beats_per_bar × 60 / bpm seconds; beats_per_bar default 4) or {seconds}, 0.5–240 s. For music WRITTEN to come round (a game level, a menu, a waiting screen: nothing ending on the last bar — the game_town and game_dungeon generators are). Send the stems as rendered, their tails past the last bar included (a render runs ~2 s past its last note): whatever still sounds at the loop point (a note's release, the room) is carried over the loop's start, and the mix is played round until its rooms and compressors have settled. The mix (and every print) comes back EXACTLY that long, to the sample: output.loop {length_s, samples, sr, seam_db}. With print_parts each part is a loop of the same length — layers that stay in time. Not with dialogue, music_offset_s or length_s.

name.description: Optional: a name for this job's files, e.g. "rainy-loop-3". Every file it returns downloads as <name>_<part>.<ext> (rainy-loop-3_Celesta.wav, rainy-loop-3_rough-mix.wav; one take: rainy-loop-3.wav), so the user can find them. Give each job its own name (a second take: "rainy-loop-3b"). Default: doseedo-<last 6 characters of the job id>.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_mix_preset
tools.description: POLISH A MIX: a mix preset is a model trained on finished, professionally mixed recordings. It covers YOUR mix and folds what it hears back in by frequency range. preset: "cinematic_score" (the default) = a whole orchestral / film-score mix, the tone and width of a finished score moved onto yours, below 8 kHz, with none of the model's own audio heard. "jazz_mix" = the same for a JAZZ mix (a combo, bossa / latin jazz — what the jazz band generators play), trained on finished jazz records: use it for those in place of cinematic_score. "big_band_mix" = the same for a BIG BAND (saxes, trumpets, trombones and a rhythm section — what the big_band_* generators play), trained on big-band records alone: use it for a big band in place of jazz_mix. Input: audio_url (a doseedo_mix mix_url as returned) or audio_key, a stereo mix of up to 10 minutes. The preset brings its own strength; cns (0.1–0.5) overrides it: how much of your mix's own sound the model's take keeps (higher = closer to the input). Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (~15–90 s) → mix_url (the polished mix, WAV), take_url (the model's raw take) and report: balance_vs_input_db per band and side_vs_input_db (the width change). Cancel: the plane has no stop for a running mix preset — it runs to completion (credits spent), the job ends as canceled and its output is discarded. Only a job still queued at the plane is refunded by the plane's own failure refund.

audio_url.description: https URL of the audio, as an alternative to audio_key: a doseedo result URL exactly as a job returned it (a stem, a take, a bounce), or any public URL. The gateway fetches it (≤256 MB) into your account's ingest storage before the job starts. Pass audio_key OR audio_url.

audio_key.description: R2 ingest key of an uploaded audio file (from doseedo_get_upload_url / POST /api/upload/r2/ingest-url; starts with "ingest/").

preset.description: The mix preset: "cinematic_score" (default) — a whole orchestral / film-score mix; "jazz_mix" — a jazz mix (combo, bossa, latin jazz); "big_band_mix" — a big band.

cns.description: The model's strength over the preset's own: how much of the input's own sound its take keeps (0.1–0.5, higher = closer to the input).

name.description: Optional: a name for this job's files, e.g. "rainy-loop-3". Every file it returns downloads as <name>_<part>.<ext> (rainy-loop-3_Celesta.wav, rainy-loop-3_rough-mix.wav; one take: rainy-loop-3.wav), so the user can find them. Give each job its own name (a second take: "rainy-loop-3b"). Default: doseedo-<last 6 characters of the job id>.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_session_from_stems
tools.description: Build a native DAW PROJECT from stems: each stem on its own audio track from bar 1, optional MIDI tracks (the written parts) beside them, on your tempo (bpm or tempo_map) — Logic Pro (.logicx) or Ableton Live (.als), zipped. The deliverable after doseedo_render_score (pass from_job: its job_id and the stems, MIDI and tempo come from that job) or after any renders / separations you made (stems: [{name, audio_url}] — result links work as-is). After doseedo_mix add mix_job: each track at that mix's level and pan, the mix as a muted reference track. Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (~30–90 s) → file (pre-signed zip, curl -o session.zip <url>, 24 h). Cancel: the plane has no stop for a running session build — it runs to completion (credits spent), the job ends as canceled and its output is discarded. Only a job still queued at the plane is refunded by the plane's own failure refund.

from_job.description: MCP: a doseedo_render_score job_id — its stems, parts' MIDI and tempo are used (no other input needed).

mix_job.description: MCP: a doseedo_mix job_id — every track takes that mix's level and pan, and the mix itself rides along as a muted reference track "Mix (doseedo)".

mixgraph.description: A mix document (doseedo_mix → mixgraph): each stem named in it takes its strip's gain_db and pan. The EQ, compression, reverb and rides are not written into the project.

stems.description: [{name, audio_url | audio_key, gain_db?, pan?, mute?, position_beats?}] — the audio tracks, in order.

midi_tracks.description: Optional MIDI tracks: [{name, notes:[{pitch, start_beats, duration_beats, velocity?}]}].

tempo_map.description: Tempo changes [{beat, bpm}] for the project.

markers.description: Arrangement markers [{name, beat}] — beat 0 = bar 1 on the project's tempo map. A scored film's cues are written as markers by `cues`.

cues.description: MCP: ONE session for a whole scored film — [{cue: "1M1", start_s, from_job: <its doseedo_render_score job>, mix_job?: <its doseedo_mix job>, emotion?}] (≤ 12 cues, from the cue sheet's start_s). Every cue's stems and MIDI land on one timeline at its start, on ONE tempo map (each cue's own tempo_map joined, each cue's bar 1 on a bar line), a marker per cue, each track at its cue's mix level and pan, each cue's mix as a muted reference. Replaces from_job / mix_job / stems.

session_beats.description: Length of the session in beats (the tempo map is written this far; default: the last note). `cues` sets it.

video.description: The film the music is written to: {video_key: the ingest/ key of your upload (doseedo_get_upload_url), name?, start_s?}. It is re-encoded lean (720p) and travels inside the project: REAPER gets a muted video track, Logic Pro gets its Movie (inside the package; Logic finds it by name). Ableton projects are built without it (the answer says so).

target.description: Which DAW (default logic): Logic Pro (.logicx), Ableton Live (.als) or REAPER (.rpp + media, with the film as a video track). Or a VIDEO EDITOR, for whoever cuts the picture: premiere (Premiere Pro: an FCP7 XML), finalcut (Final Cut Pro: an FCPXML) or resolve (DaVinci Resolve: both). An editor project is the film on V1, every stem as its own clip at its position (one track per part across the cues), a marker per cue, the sequence at the film's own start timecode, with its media beside it (48 kHz, 24-bit). Each stem's gain_db and pan are printed into its file, so clips sit at unity; midi_tracks and the tempo map are not written (a timeline holds none).

name.description: Project name — the project inside the zip, and the zip itself downloads as <name>_session.zip.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_spot_video
tools.description: SPOT A FILM: a video in, the music editor's cue sheet out — the first step of scoring to picture. Scene detection on EVERY frame, and it listens to the soundtrack (CPU, no credits): hard cuts frame-exact (dark, low-contrast footage included), fades, flashes and visual impacts; each shot's brightness, colour, warmth, contrast, motion and mood, with a keyframe JPEG per shot so you can SEE what it shows; SCENES — where the picture moves to a new place, at a cut or with none (a camera move, a dissolve) — each with its start, how it arrives, how fast the camera travels (pace) and a 640-px frame; and a storyboard: the whole film on one JPEG, a frame every few seconds; where dialogue is (Silero VAD) and loud audio hits; INTENSITY — the picture's energy (motion, cutting, camera, the sound) as sections [{start_s, end_s, level, rel: low | medium | high | peak}] (≤ 30 s each; peak only where the level reads high), and each scene's own (section_rel: its level on the steps alone, for the cue layout): where the music steps up, settles and peaks; then cues placed where the picture wants music and the dialogue lets it (1M1, 1M2 …: start/end SMPTE timecode, emotion, energy, tension arc, hit points ranked by strength, a suggested bpm that lands them, and tempo_map_input — pass it to doseedo_tempo_map as is). It sees light, movement and editing, not meaning: read the scene frames and the storyboard for what each scene is about. Input: video_key (doseedo_get_upload_url accepts mp4/mov/m4v/webm/mkv) or video_url (public https), ≤ 2 GB and ≤ 3 h. Optional start_timecode (the first frame's, e.g. 01:00:00:00; default the file's own), coverage (0.05–0.98, default 0.55: how much of the film gets music), reel (cue ids <reel>M<n>), keyframes (0–60), spotter. Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (~1 min for a 10-min 1080p reel). Next: doseedo_tempo_map per cue → write the notes → doseedo_render_score → doseedo_mix → doseedo_score_to_picture. Cancel: a spotting pass still queued never starts and one running stops within seconds; either way its credit is refunded and the job ends as canceled.

video_key.description: R2 ingest key of the uploaded video (doseedo_get_upload_url with the file name, e.g. reel1.mp4; starts with "ingest/").

video_url.description: https URL of the video, as an alternative to video_key (a public file URL, fetched directly; ≤ 2 GB).

start_timecode.description: SMPTE timecode of the first frame, HH:MM:SS:FF (";" before the frames = drop-frame at 29.97/59.94). Default: the file's embedded timecode, else 00:00:00:00.

coverage.description: How much of the film gets music (default 0.55). Raise it for wall-to-wall scoring (a trailer, an animation), lower it for a dialogue drama.

reel.description: Reel number for the cue ids (default 1 → 1M1, 1M2 …).

keyframes.description: How many shots get a keyframe JPEG (default 24; the longest shots first). 0 = no images at all (no scene frames, no storyboard).

cut_threshold.description: Scene-change threshold at full contrast (default 0.3). Lower finds softer cuts, higher only the hardest.

spotter.description: Who places the cues. "rules" (default): light, motion and editing, weighted by hand, at coverage. "model": a cue model trained on 200 human-scored films. It places the cues where a composer would, and gives each cue its tempo (suggested_bpm), dynamics marks (dynamics: pp–ff every 8 s), turns (where it comes in full or steps up or down) and hits. Its tempo_map_input lands the hits on a beat and the turns on a bar line. Without coverage it decides how much of the film gets music; cue_sheet.cue_model says what it decided.

name.description: Optional: a name for this job's files, e.g. "rainy-loop-3". Every file it returns downloads as <name>_<part>.<ext> (rainy-loop-3_Celesta.wav, rainy-loop-3_rough-mix.wav; one take: rainy-loop-3.wav), so the user can find them. Give each job its own name (a second take: "rainy-loop-3b"). Default: doseedo-<last 6 characters of the job id>.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_score_to_picture
tools.description: SCORE TO PICTURE: the last step of scoring a film. Lays each mixed cue (and any sound effect) on the video at its SMPTE timecode, with dialogue ducking (the lines found on the video's own soundtrack by VAD, or the spans you pass; the music dips ahead of each line and comes back after it), normalises the program to a delivery loudness (web −16, streaming −14, broadcast/ebu −23, atsc −24 LUFS, or a number; true peak under the ceiling) and muxes it onto the picture untouched (no re-encode). Returns the scored video, the printmaster WAV and the music-and-effects stem, plus a report of what it MEASURED: where each track landed (and what was cut at the film's edges), how far the music sits under the lines, and the final loudness and true peak. CPU, no credits. tracks: [{audio_url (a doseedo_mix mix_url as returned, or any public https URL) | audio_key, start_timecode (in the film's timecode) | start_s, gain_db?, role?: music|dialogue|effects, duck?, name?}], ≤ 64. Keep the production audio (default) or drop it (production_audio:"drop"). A FILM THAT ALREADY HAS MUSIC: keeping its audio mixes the old music under yours — split it first (doseedo_split_soundtrack) and lay its dialogue and effects stems back (start_s 0, role dialogue / effects) with production_audio:"drop": the old music is gone, the lines are kept, and the duck reads the lines off the dialogue stem; lay the old music stem back too with duck:false to keep it (or a part of it). With dialogue tracks the delivery also returns the dialogue / music / effects stems. report.tracks[] names each placed track's role (none said is music; sfx is effects): a delivery that placed NO music (a film of its sound design alone) still returns score and music files, which are silence — hand over the printmaster instead. Up to 25 minutes of film per call (a reel). Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task. Cancel: a delivery still queued never starts and one running stops within seconds; either way its credit is refunded and the job ends as canceled.

video_key.description: R2 ingest key of the video (the same upload doseedo_spot_video used).

video_url.description: https URL of the video, as an alternative to video_key.

tracks.description: What to lay on the film, in any order.

audio_url.description: The cue's mixed audio (doseedo_mix mix_url as returned) or any public https URL.

audio_key.description: An ingest key instead of audio_url.

start_timecode.description: Where it starts, in the film's timecode (HH:MM:SS:FF) — the cue sheet's start_timecode.

start_s.description: Or where it starts in seconds from the first frame (negative = its head is before the first frame and cut there).

source_start_s.description: Where in the AUDIO it starts playing (default 0): pick the stretch of a longer piece — a public-domain recording cut to a :30 starts at the phrase you chose. The cut is faded (declick).

length_s.description: How much of the audio plays from source_start_s (default: to its end or the last frame). The cut is faded (declick).

fade_in_s.description: A longer fade in from its first heard sample (the first frame when its head is cut).

fade_out_s.description: A longer fade out to its last heard sample — its own end, length_s, or the last frame: let a piece go over the last shot instead of cutting it.

repeat_every_s.description: A LOOP: lay this audio again every this many seconds (its period, to the millisecond — a loop of N bars at one fixed tempo: N × beats per bar × 60 / bpm) until repeat_until_s. The file may be longer than its period: its tail rings over the seam. For music that repeats verbatim (a vamp, a bed, a picture that is itself a loop: the cue sheet's video.picture_loop) — render and mix the loop ONCE instead of every stem for the whole length. receipt: tracks[].repeats.

repeat_until_s.description: With repeat_every_s: no copy starts at or after this film second (default: the last frame).

gain_db.description: Level trim (default 0), on top of the cue's seat. Every doseedo_mix is mastered to one loudness, a lone part's as a whole band's, so each music cue is laid at its share of the fullest cue in the delivery (at most four parts): a guitar mixed alone laid over or between a duo's cues sits 3 dB under its master, under a band of four or more 6 dB (folk records hold one part of the band at an equal share); the fullest cue, and a film scored by one part alone, play as mastered. report.tracks[].texture {parts, seat_db} says what it read and moved. Leave gain_db at 0 for that place; trim from there.

as_mastered.description: true = lay this cue at its own master, never at its share of the fullest cue (a solo cue meant to stand as loud as the full score).

role.description: music (default; ducked under the dialogue), dialogue (never ducked — the lines the rest ducks under; a split soundtrack's dialogue stem), effects / sfx (not ducked unless duck.sfx).

duck.description: false = this music track is not ducked: a band seen playing in the scene or a drop (the scene's own sound, forward), or the film's own music laid back from doseedo_split_soundtrack (mixed under its lines already). Default true.

medium.description: false = never printed in the film's medium (see medium): the film's own music laid back from doseedo_split_soundtrack is in it already. Default true.

name.description: A label for the report, e.g. 1M3.

start_timecode.description: SMPTE timecode of the film's first frame (default: the file's own, else 00:00:00:00) — the clock the tracks' start_timecode is read on.

duck.description: Dialogue ducking (on by default): depth_db (default: line by line, the music is HELD 15–18 dB under the voice that line is spoken at, by a LEVEL and a gentle dip — each passage of talk under a cue SEATS the cue lower (a fader ride, from the cue's head when the talk starts near it; music with no talk near it is never lowered) and each line dips a few dB on top (6, at most 9: report duck.depth_db; held_under_lines.seated_db, deepest_db = both, up to 24; tracks[].seated_db), lifted back where it sits deeper, never above the cue as mixed; the voice is read on the dialogue tracks, else on the film's own audio when it is kept (its bed beside each line taken off), and a kept film audio whose voices are too quiet to hold the music under is raised by up to 12 dB — as far as the print master's limiter can hold its own peaks, the dip deepening by what the lift cannot give — unless production_gain_db says; the music never dips under the film audio's ROOM beside a line (its noise, its own music left out, lifted with the voice: held_under_lines.room_db / lines_at_room); lines closer than attack + release are one stretch, and a dip moves at most 6 dB between lines a breath apart; a depth you give is used as given and switches the hold off), under_voice_db (the hold's target, 0–40, default 15: how far under the voices the music is held — the window runs from it to 3 dB more, the seat moving with it, seat and dip to 24 in all, deeper by as much as the target is past 15 (to 40); a note asking for the music further back raises it; the report says the depth used, music_under_dialogue_db (music minus the voices, measured), under_voice_db and held_under_lines), attack_ms (250: how early before a line the music is down), release_ms (700), sfx (false: duck effects too), enabled.

dialogue.description: Dialogue spans [{start_s, end_s}] to duck under, instead of detecting them (use the cue sheet's dialogue, or your own).

loudness.description: Delivery loudness: "web" (−16 LUFS, default), "streaming" (−14), "broadcast" / "ebu" (−23), "atsc" (−24), or a LUFS number (−36…−8).

production_audio.description: keep (default) mixes the video's own soundtrack — all of it, its music included — under the score; drop replaces it (lay a doseedo_split_soundtrack's dialogue + effects stems to keep the lines).

production_gain_db.description: Trim on the production audio when kept (default: 0, lifted by up to 12 where its voices are too quiet to hold the music under; a value you give is used as given).

loudness_gain_db.description: The print-master gain of an earlier delivery of this film (its report.loudness.gain_db): kept, so the cues this version did not touch play at the level they had, while the program lands within ±1 LU of its target; else this program's own gain (report.loudness.gain_lock says which).

medium.description: THE FILM'S OWN RECORDING MEDIUM: a period film's music and lines were recorded on the medium of their day (mono, the highs ending by 9 kHz, no deep bass), and a modern hi-fi score sounds wrong beside them. Pass doseedo_split_soundtrack's soundtrack.medium AS IT CAME when it reads period: every music track (not medium:false) is printed in it — a high-pass and low-pass fitted on each cue so its spectrum lands on the film's own skirt points, folded to the film's width, peaks rounded to the film music's, its loudness kept — and the music is held under the lines as far as the film's own sat (placement; duck.under_voice_db wins). {period: true} alone = the shellac medium (a 1940s transfer's band, mono, surface noise) for a director who asks for the old-record sound on a film that does not read as one; {period: false} = the modern sound, nothing printed. report.medium + tracks[].medium say what was printed and where each cue's skirts landed against the film's.

print.description: As read (soundtrack.medium.print): top_hz [Hz at −15 dB, at −30 dB under the body], low_hz [at −10, at −20], fall_db, mono, side_db, crest_db.

placement.description: As read: {music_under_dialogue_db} — how far under its lines the film's own music sat.

said.description: The director's own words that ask for the sound (old record, period, modern, hi-fi), copied exactly.

tools.name: doseedo_sound_design
tools.description: SOUND DESIGN for a film, from a PLAN of its sound: beds (a place's sound per scene — near and far) and events (each one a STACK of layers by its kind: an impact = hit + lead-in + debris + weight; a whoosh = body + speed + character; footsteps; a riser…), every sound named in a sound library's words (3–6 plain words: source, material, action). TWO CALLS: (1) {video_key, plan} → asks: the sounds the plan needs, each once — make each with doseedo_generate_sound {prompt, kind, duration_seconds} — its prompt, never its ask (10 credits a sound); (2) the same {video_key, plan} + sounds: [{ask, audio_url}] → the plan's times snapped onto the picture (its cuts, in-shot impacts and movements), every layer placed, levelled, panned, in its room, and the SESSION: lanes[] = the FX bus's tracks, one per type of sound (Ambience, Footsteps, Impacts, Whooshes, Risers…) and, where a type is layered, one per layer ("Impacts · hit", "Impacts · debris"), each a file over the whole film (url) with its regions [{start_s, end_s}] and the fader it plays at (gain_db); mix_url = the whole design as one stem — lay it on the film with doseedo_score_to_picture tracks [{audio_url: mix_url, start_s: 0, role: "effects"}], and hand the lanes over as the session's tracks (a film of sound design alone: its download is the printmaster and these, never the silent score). A sound that is not sent is left out and listed (report.missing). CPU, no credits. Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (the first call ~1 s, the second ~20–90 s: it reads every frame). Cancel: a sound design still queued never starts and one running stops within seconds; either way its credit is refunded and the job ends as canceled.

plan.description: The sound of the film: {beds: [{from, to, near, far?, level?: low|mid|high, fade_in?, fade_out?}], events: [{at, kind, size?: 1|2|3, what, pan?: -1..1, layers?: {<layer>: words}} | {kind: "steps", from, to, people?: 1-4, what}]} — seconds on the film; kind = whoosh | pass | impact | mechanism | hard | accent | ui | group | creature | rise | steps.

sounds.description: The second call: each ask the first call returned, with the sound made for it — [{ask, audio_url}] (a doseedo_generate_sound file URL as returned).

tools.name: doseedo_reframe_video
tools.description: REFRAME A VIDEO: the same video in another frame, for where it is posted — 9:16 (stories, reels, shorts), 4:5 (a feed post), 1:1 (square) or 16:9 (a landscape master). fit "fit" (default) keeps the whole picture, centred over a blurred fill of itself, so nothing is cut (captions at the top or bottom of a vertical ad stay); "fill" scales to cover the frame and centre-crops the rest (the report says how much of the picture is kept). The sound is kept as it is (a scored film's mix untouched). Up to 1080 px on the short side (never upscaled past the source's), H.264 MP4. A video already in that frame is copied, not re-encoded. Input: video_key (an upload) or video_url (a doseedo_score_to_picture video as returned, or any public https URL). CPU, no credits. Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task. tools.name: doseedo_cover_song
tools.description: AI COVER / style transfer of a whole song: re-render an uploaded song as a cover, keeping its structure/melody while changing timbre, instruments, or lyrics. INSTRUMENT SWAP: instruments {"piano": "electric_guitar"} separates the song, transcribes the swapped stem and re-plays THOSE transcribed notes on the target instrument; by default only the swapped stem(s) are regenerated and every other stem passes through as the original separated audio (regen changes that). Because the swap replays a transcription, small note differences from the source are expected — verify from result.cover.instrument_swaps (applied or why not), and offer the user the result/takes to judge rather than promising a note-perfect copy. Target ids: GET https://api.doseedo.com/api/instruments (open). Optionally export a DAW session too. Async: returns a job_id — poll with doseedo_wait_task (several minutes for full songs). Result files are pre-signed links: curl -OJ <url>, no auth header (valid 24 h). Cancel: a render that has not reached the GPU yet is stopped and its credits refunded; one already rendering finishes on the GPU (its credits are spent), the job ends as canceled and the output is discarded.

audio_key.description: R2 ingest key of an uploaded audio file (from doseedo_get_upload_url / POST /api/upload/r2/ingest-url; starts with "ingest/"). Provide this or audio_url.

audio_url.description: https URL of the audio, as an alternative to audio_key: a doseedo result URL exactly as a job returned it (a stem, a take, a bounce), or any public URL. The gateway fetches it (≤256 MB) into your account's ingest storage before the job starts. Pass audio_key OR audio_url.

genre.description: Optional GENRE style transfer: the target genre in a few words, ≤ 64 characters (e.g. "bossa nova", "80s synth-pop", "West End musical showstopper") — a name, not a description; a longer one is cut at its last comma or word that fits, with a warning on the reply. Every regenerated stem is captioned with it. Outcome in result.cover.genre.

style_key.description: Optional ingest key (upload it first) of a reference MIX whose TIMBRE the regenerated stems take on (style transfer).

structure_key.description: Optional ingest key of audio whose STRUCTURE codes replace the source's (the Cover page's "Structure: custom").

timbre_preset.description: Optional named timbre preset — the fallback rung of the timbre ladder (stem latent > this > stock bank).

drum_split.description: true = explode the covered drums into isolated kick/snare/hh/… stems, each generated from its own slice of the drum roll (result.drum_stems).

guitar_split.description: Deal the guitar bucket into N players, each its own row/swap: "2"–"4", or "auto" (a one-vs-two probe decides). Outcome in result.cover.guitar_split.

instruments.description: Optional per-stem instrument SWAP map {source: target}, e.g. {"piano": "electric_guitar", "sax": "violin"}. Source = a stem (drums, bass, vocals, guitar, piano, other) or a detected instrument (sax, trumpet…); target = an instrument id from /api/instruments (an unknown target is refused up front).

cover_noise_strength.description: Optional 0–1 fidelity dial: higher departs further from the source.

swap_cns.description: Optional 0–1, only with instruments: how far the SWAPPED stems may depart from their source (overrides cover_noise_strength for them; server default 0.35). Lower = closer to the original timing/feel.

regen.description: Optional: which stems to regenerate. Default with a swap = only the swapped stems (the rest are the original separated audio). "all" = cover every stem; or a comma list of stems/instruments, e.g. "piano,other" (a swapped stem is always regenerated).

labels.description: Optional identity CORRECTIONS {source: instrument}, same shape as instruments, e.g. {"other": "trumpet"} when the separation mislabels a stem. Only fixes what the stem is called (caption/timbre); nothing is re-played. Outcome in result.cover.stem_labels.

midi_only.description: Optional: re-perform every regenerated stem from its transcribed MIDI with NO timbre from the recording (the stem's own sound is dropped). Stems with nothing to render are skipped (result.cover.midi_only.skipped).

export.description: Optionally also build a DAW session for this target.

tools.name: doseedo_separate_stems
tools.description: STEM SEPARATION and VOCAL REMOVER: split an uploaded mix into stems (vocals, drums, bass, guitar, piano, other — or orchestral/auto-detected instruments) to isolate vocals (the vocals stem is the acapella; the other stems are the karaoke backing), with optional per-stem MIDI transcription and DAW-session export. Async: returns a job_id — poll with doseedo_wait_task (~2 minutes). Result: stems{name: url}, midi{name: url}, drum_substems{kick, snare, …} (drum_split), vocals_lyrics / vocals_notes, session_tracks + session_tempo_bpm when session_id was given, models_effective (what the auto family gate actually ran), other_classification (what the "other" stem was heard as), guitar_split (outcome). Cancel: the plane has no stop for a running separation — it runs to completion (credits spent), the job ends as canceled and its output is discarded. Only a job still queued at the plane is refunded by the plane's own failure refund.

audio_key.description: R2 ingest key of an uploaded audio file (from doseedo_get_upload_url / POST /api/upload/r2/ingest-url; starts with "ingest/"). Provide this or audio_url.

audio_url.description: https URL of the audio, as an alternative to audio_key: a doseedo result URL exactly as a job returned it (a stem, a take, a bounce), or any public URL. The gateway fetches it (≤256 MB) into your account's ingest storage before the job starts. Pass audio_key OR audio_url.

models.description: Separation model set. Default 6stem (vocals/drums/bass/guitar/piano/other); auto/orchestra/detect for wider instrument sets.

section_stems.description: models=auto only: how a record's sections come back once auto hears them in "other". "families" = brass / woodwind / strings as one stem each (the cleaner split; the stems add up to the "other" they came from), "instruments" = trumpet / trombone / sax / violin / viola / cello heads. Omit for the service default (instruments). One instrument alone is models=orchestra + instruments.

instruments.description: models=orchestra only: comma-separated extractor targets, e.g. "saxophone,trumpet,trombone". Available: drums, percussion, bass, double_bass, guitar, electric_guitar, acoustic_guitar, piano, organ, harp, brass, trumpet, trombone, french_horn, tuba, saxophone, clarinet, oboe, bassoon, flute, woodwind, strings, violin, viola, cello. Omit for the curated default set. Names as people write them are read onto these ("Trumpets", "french horn", "trompettes et trombones", "alto sax" → saxophone); result.instruments_asked says what each name became: asked[] {asked, target, exact (false = heard inside that stem with what else it holds), note "kit" = a drum kit's piece (the drums stem; drum_split deals the kit out)}, not_separated[] {asked, why: voice (use models 6stem) | other (a vibraphone / marimba / xylophone has no extractor; it stays in the 6stem "other") | synth | ambiguous | unknown}. Names none of which has an extractor = a 400, no charge.

include_midi.description: Also transcribe each stem to MIDI (default true).

stems_only.description: true = the stems and NOTHING derived from them (no MIDI, no lyrics, no latents) — the fastest, cheapest separation. Implies include_midi:false.

drum_split.description: true = also split the drum stem into isolated kick / snare / hi-hat / toms / ride / crash (+ perc) sub-stems (result.drum_substems).

guitar_split.description: Deal the guitar stem into N players (same-instrument separation): "2"–"4", or "auto" (a one-vs-two probe decides; no split when it hears one). Outcome in result.guitar_split.

tools.name: doseedo_split_soundtrack
tools.description: SPLIT A FILM'S SOUNDTRACK (dialogue / music / effects — "DME" — separation): the film's own audio into three stems that sum back to it, plus a report of what it holds: whether there is music already, where it plays (spans in seconds) and how much of the film it covers, where the dialogue is (cleaner than VAD on the full mix: a song's singer stays in the music stem), where the film's own music is loudest (stems.music.peaks: its climaxes), a click track the cut was made to (pulse: {start_s, end_s, bpm}; its clicks are no impacts), each part's level, and how far the music sits under the lines. Use it before scoring a film that already has music (soundtrack.stems.music.present): to REPLACE that music, lay the dialogue and effects stems under your score with doseedo_score_to_picture (production_audio:"drop", tracks role "dialogue" / "effects"); to REMIX or RE-ORCHESTRATE it, the music stem goes to doseedo_separate_stems / doseedo_transcribe / doseedo_analyze_song; to KEEP it, score where the report shows no music. Input: video_key (the upload doseedo_spot_video read) or video_url; audio_key / audio_url for a soundtrack already on its own. One reel per call (≤ 30 min). The split is good, not perfect: a line the separator heard as music is moved back to the dialogue (soundtrack.dialogue_rescue says what moved; a sung or rapped voice stays in the music as the film's song), while some of the old music (its percussion most) reads as effects — about −10 dB of it stays in the dialogue + effects bed, which the new score masks. Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (about a third of the soundtrack's length: a 3-min scene ≈ 1 min, a 20-min reel ≈ 6 min). Cancel: the plane has no stop for a running split — it runs to completion (credits spent), the job ends as canceled and its output is discarded. Only a job still queued at the plane is refunded by the plane's own failure refund.

video_url.description: https URL of the film, as an alternative to video_key (fetched through the URL up to 256 MB; upload a bigger film).
