tools.name: doseedo_transcribe
tools.description: AUDIO TO MIDI transcription: a melody, a bass line or a part as notes (pitch, onset/offset seconds, velocity, confidence as JSON — not a MIDI file; for .mid files per stem use doseedo_separate_stems with transcription or doseedo_audio_to_session). Works from an uploaded audio_key or an audio_url — any public https URL, including a result URL from another doseedo job (a generate take, a stem) as it was returned. Async: returns a job_id — poll with doseedo_wait_task (usually ~15–60s). For the KEY / tempo / chords of a whole mix use doseedo_analyze_song instead. Cancel: the plane has no stop for a running transcription — it runs to completion (credits spent), the job ends as canceled and its output is discarded. Only a job still queued at the plane is refunded by the plane's own failure refund.

audio_key.description: R2 ingest key of an uploaded audio file (from doseedo_get_upload_url / POST /api/upload/r2/ingest-url; starts with "ingest/"). Provide this or audio_url.

audio_url.description: https URL of the audio to transcribe (alternative to audio_key): any public URL, or a doseedo result URL exactly as a job returned it — no key needed.

tempo_bpm.description: Optional known tempo — enables beat-aligned note times.

register.description: Optional register hint for the instrument (e.g. "soprano", "tenor", "bass").

family.description: Optional instrument family (e.g. "brass", "reeds", "strings") when the exact instrument is unknown.

polyphony.description: Optional: "solo" (monophonic line), "poly", or "section" (a horn section — see roster/chairs).

roster.description: polyphony="section": the chairs on the stem, e.g. "trumpet,trumpet,trombone,tenor_sax". Omit for the family default.

chairs.description: polyphony="section": register codes per chair, as an alternative to roster.

strikes.description: With tempo_bpm: also return the harmony_strikes attack grid.

beats_per_bar.description: With tempo_bpm: beats per bar for the beat-domain times (default 4).

backend.description: Advanced: force a transcription backend. Omit — the server routes by instrument.

want.description: What to return: "notes" (default), "f0" (the continuous pitch contour — frame-rate Hz values, for glides/vibrato/intonation), or both.

record_tuning.description: Optional: the tuning of the RECORD this stem came off, in cents off A=440 (+ sharp) — e.g. record_tuning.cents of a doseedo_separate_stems result. A stem is measured and read in its own tuning either way; one that cannot be measured alone (too little playing, its passages disagree) is read in the record's instead of at A440. result.meta.tuning.from says which: "stem" or "record".

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_audio_to_session
tools.description: Turn an uploaded full mix into a complete multitrack DAW session (separated stems as tracks, tempo map, optional per-stem MIDI and chord guide). The result is a downloadable session zip for Logic Pro or Ableton. Async: returns a job_id — poll with doseedo_wait_task (~4 minutes). Cancel: cooperative — the build stops at its next stage boundary and the build's sound-tool unit is refunded (a GPU separation already run stays charged).

audio_key.description: R2 ingest key of an uploaded audio file (from doseedo_get_upload_url / POST /api/upload/r2/ingest-url; starts with "ingest/"). Provide this or audio_url.

audio_url.description: https URL of the audio, as an alternative to audio_key: a doseedo result URL exactly as a job returned it (a stem, a take, a bounce), or any public URL. The gateway fetches it (≤256 MB) into your account's ingest storage before the job starts. Pass audio_key OR audio_url.

midi_stems.description: Optional comma-separated stems to also add as MIDI tracks, e.g. "piano,bass" (include "drums" for a GM drum roll).

keep_stem_audio.description: With midi_stems: keep the audio stem next to its MIDI track (default true); false = the MIDI track REPLACES the audio.

chords.description: Add a detected-chords guide track (default false).

key.description: Detect the key and write it into the project (default true in the full build, false with simple).

markers.description: Add section markers (intro/verse/chorus…) (default true in the full build, false with simple).

simple.description: Faster minimal build: meter + tempo + stems only, no MIDI (default false). Required for stem_mode orchestra/detect.

separate.description: false = no separation: the mix lands as ONE audio track (default true).

tempo_map.description: false = one constant tempo instead of a tempo map (default true).

stem_mode.description: Separation family. auto (DEFAULT): the 6 stems plus a residual cascade that peels detected orchestral sections out of "other" (no orchestral content → identical to 6stem). 6stem: vocals/drums/bass/guitar/piano/other. drumsep: the drum stem replaced by isolated kick/snare/hh/… tracks on a Drums bus. sections: the 6 stems with "other" split by the joint section model (trumpet/trombone/sax/violin/viola/cello), each transcribed per chair. orchestra / detect: the 53-instrument bank on the MIX (needs simple:true; detect auto-picks, orchestra takes `instruments`).

instruments.description: stem_mode orchestra/detect: optional comma list restricting the orchestral set, e.g. "violin,cello,flute" (the doseedo_separate_stems instruments targets; names as people write them are read onto those, and summary.stages[] "separation" carries instruments_asked: what each name became, or why nothing extracts it).

quantize_midi.description: Snap every pitched MIDI lane: "grid" = to the grid its own onsets support (straight/swing 8ths, 16ths, triplets, detected per lane); "score" = notation positions (straight 8ths). Default off (played timing).

drum_substems.description: Lay each drum piece as its own audio track on a Drums bus (default false; implied by stem_mode drumsep).

drum_midi_split.description: With "drums" in midi_stems: one Quick Sampler track PER kit piece, each loaded with a synthesized one-shot (default false = one GM drum-roll track).

guitar_split.description: Split the guitar stem into N players, each its own track + MIDI lane on a Guitar Section bus: "0" (off), "auto" (DEFAULT — a one-vs-two probe decides), "2"–"4".

retune.description: Default true: a mix sitting >35 cents off A440 is pitch-corrected onto the 12-TET grid before separation (every transcriber coin-flips otherwise). false = leave the tuning as recorded.

dereverb.description: Opt-in: lay DRY stems and recreate the room with a reverb plugin on each track (default false).

crop_silence.description: Punch regions in where each stem plays instead of whole-length stems (default false).

loops.description: Detect repeated clips and lay them as loops (default false).

drum_sampler.description: Sampled kits → a one-shot sampler track + MIDI (default false).

name.description: Project name for the session file — it also names the download: <name>_session.zip.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_convert_project
tools.description: DAW CONVERTER: a project rebuilt natively in the target: tracks, MIDI, audio clips, tempo and markers arrive editable (Logic/Ableton/Pro Tools/REAPER pairs also automation, buses/sends, plugin state; into FL 3rd-party plugins only). Sources: Logic .logicx, Ableton .als, FL Studio .flp, Pro Tools .ptx, REAPER .rpp, Cubase .cpr, Dorico .dorico/.musicxml, Studio One .song, GarageBand .band (SOURCE only — zip the .band package like a .logicx; a GarageBand 6 project must be re-saved in GarageBand 10), Bitwig = any .dawproject (Bitwig/Studio One/Cubase export it; a native .bwproject is refused — File > Export… > DAWproject in Bitwig). The enum lists the exact pairs. ★ ASYMMETRIC TARGETS (an undocumented native file is never written): TO Cubase, Studio One or Bitwig = ONE .dawproject the app imports, not a .cpr/.song/.bwproject; TO Dorico = MusicXML (.mxl, Dorico's own notation import), not a .dorico. FROM Cubase the .cpr carries tracks, tempo and MIDI parts but not the audio pool (audio tracks arrive empty). FROM Dorico a .dorico carries players and flows but NOT its notes: convert its MusicXML export instead (.musicxml/.mxl accepted under dorico2*). Every result carries a transfer REPORT: `report`, `lossy`, `summary[]` (what changed), `warnings[]` (read before opening) — relay them; silence is never "lossless". Upload first: doseedo_get_project_upload_url + PUT (zip a project FOLDER so its audio travels; a bare project file works too; multipart past ~4 GB). Directions: "<source>2<target>"; "auto2<target>" detects the source; "<daw>2<daw>" rebuilds Logic/Ableton/FL/REAPER/Pro Tools in place (e.g. options.third_party_plugins:"disable"). To EDIT a project use doseedo_import_project; to convert a session the tools built: doseedo_download_session → upload that zip → logic2<target> (not a session_id). Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (15 s–2 min; `stage`); `file` is a direct storage link. Cancel: no stop — it completes, the job ends canceled, output discarded; the credit is refunded only when the conversion itself fails.

project_key.description: R2 key of the uploaded project (from doseedo_get_project_upload_url / POST /api/upload/r2/signed-url; starts with "uploads/").

direction.description: Source and target as "<source>2<target>" (logic | ableton | fl | protools | reaper | cubase | dorico | studioone | bitwig | garageband | aaf), "auto2<target>" to let the server detect the source, or "<daw>2<daw>" to rebuild in the same format (Logic/Ableton/FL/REAPER/Pro Tools only). cubase2* reads a .cpr and *2cubase writes a .dawproject (Cubase 14+/Nuendo open it natively). dorico2* reads a .dorico, .musicxml or .mxl and *2dorico writes MusicXML (.mxl). studioone2* reads a .song and *2studioone writes a .dawproject (Studio One 6.5+ imports it). bitwig2* reads any .dawproject and *2bitwig writes a .dawproject (Bitwig 5+ imports it). garageband2* reads a zipped .band package (source only — no *2garageband). aaf2* reads an AAF (Pro Tools / Logic / Resolve / Premiere export) — zip the .aaf with its audio files so clips relink by name; audio only, every clip unwarped at its exact time, no *2aaf or aaf2dorico.

options.description: Conversion options (all optional). third_party_plugins:"disable" drops third-party AU/VST devices so the export opens clean on a machine without them; stock_plugins:"disable" leaves stock devices unmapped instead of mapping to the nearest target-DAW device; carry_plugin_presets:false strips plugin patches; lossless:true (→Logic) pins the project to the MAX clip sample rate so no clip is downsampled; project_rate (→Logic) pins an exact rate in Hz; silence_empty_sampler:false (→Logic) keeps Logic's audible default Quick Sampler on tracks whose sampler had no sample; source_name = the project's display name for the output file.

source_name.description: Display name of the source project, e.g. "My Song.als" — names the output.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_analyze_song
tools.description: Key detection, BPM/tempo detection, song structure and chords — musical analysis of a recording in one call: key (e.g. "D minor"), bpm + per-beat tempo_map, meter / beats_per_bar, downbeats (seconds), sections (intro/verse/chorus… with times), chords (a progression on the beat grid), dynamics, and cues: the pieces a recording holds (a film's temp: each piece's start, end, tempo, key and level). USE THIS to learn the key and tempo of a reference before writing a part — never guess or ask the user for what the audio already says. Pass audio_key (an upload) or audio_url (a result URL from another job as returned, or any public https URL). Up to 10 minutes of audio is analyzed. Synchronous (~5–20 s for a song, up to ~1–2 min for 10 minutes of audio): the result is in this response. No separation, so a dense mix's chords are a draft — for a chord chart from stems use doseedo_detect_chords on the separated stems. Cancel: not applicable — the result is returned in the submit response; the job is already finished.

audio_key.description: R2 ingest key of an uploaded audio file (from doseedo_get_upload_url / POST /api/upload/r2/ingest-url; starts with "ingest/"). Provide this or audio_url.

audio_url.description: https URL of the audio (a doseedo result URL as returned, or any public URL). Alternative to audio_key.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_detect_chords
tools.description: Chord detection on audio (a chord chart on the beat grid): chord_spans[{chord, start, end, start_beat, end_beat, confidence}], chords{"<beat>": "Am7"}, bpm, beats_per_bar, beat_map. Default = the deep ACE detector (GPU-backed, a CPU chroma detector is the automatic fallback); deep:false forces the fast CPU detector. Pass audio_key (an upload) or audio_url (a result URL from another job as returned, or any public https URL). Up to 10 minutes of audio is analyzed. Works best on a harmonic stem (piano/guitar/bass) or a clean mix. Synchronous (~5–30 s). Cancel: not applicable — the result is returned in the submit response; the job is already finished.

audio_key.description: R2 ingest key of an uploaded audio file (from doseedo_get_upload_url / POST /api/upload/r2/ingest-url; starts with "ingest/"). Provide this or audio_url.

audio_url.description: https URL of the audio (a doseedo result URL as returned, or any public URL). Alternative to audio_key.

deep.description: true (default) = deep ACE detector; false = fast CPU chroma detector.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_beat_grid
tools.description: Beat detection / beat tracking: bpm, beats[] (seconds), downbeats[] (seconds), beats_per_bar, downbeat_offset, beat_map[{t, pos}], duration — the grid to place a part against a recording (beat n is at beats[n] seconds). Pass audio_key (an upload) or audio_url (a result URL from another job as returned, or any public https URL). Up to 10 minutes of audio is analyzed. Synchronous (~3–15 s). For key + sections + chords as well use doseedo_analyze_song. Cancel: not applicable — the result is returned in the submit response; the job is already finished.

audio_key.description: R2 ingest key of an uploaded audio file (from doseedo_get_upload_url / POST /api/upload/r2/ingest-url; starts with "ingest/"). Provide this or audio_url.

audio_url.description: https URL of the audio (a doseedo result URL as returned, or any public URL). Alternative to audio_key.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_identify_sound
tools.description: Instrument recognition + genre classification of audio (a stem, a loop, a whole mix): instrument (e.g. "sub_bass", "drum_machine", "synth_lead", "string_section"), family, render (the doseedo_render_midi fields that play it), write (how its part is written), candidates[], resembles[] (what it sounds like without being it: a synth lead that resembles a brass section), confidence, notes {low, high, most} (its register), genre[] (top 3), character {tone bright|dark, drive clean|driven, length short|sustained, weight}, reads (playful | neutral | sleek: does it sound like a toy advert or a cartoon?) + playful 0–1, tags[] (AudioSet) and measured {rms_dbfs, centroid_hz, low_share, onsets_per_s}. USE THIS on a reference track and on each of its stems (doseedo_separate_stems returns stem_identity already) before writing: you cannot hear, and tempo and key say nothing about the SOUND. Run it on your own mix too and compare genre and character with the reference. A whole mix: read genre and character (instrument names only its loudest element). A silent stem answers silent:true — nothing to copy there. Pass audio_key (an upload) or audio_url (a result URL from another job as returned, or any public https URL). Up to 10 minutes of audio is analyzed. Synchronous (~1–5 s), no credits. Cancel: not applicable — the result is returned in the submit response; the job is already finished.

audio_key.description: R2 ingest key of an uploaded audio file (from doseedo_get_upload_url / POST /api/upload/r2/ingest-url; starts with "ingest/"). Provide this or audio_url.

audio_url.description: https URL of the audio (a doseedo result URL as returned — a stem, a take — or any public URL). Alternative to audio_key.

want.description: Which answers to compute (default all three).

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_check_take
tools.description: MEASURE a take instead of guessing: give the audio (a render_midi take URL, any recording) and the notes it should play — notes[] + bpm (and tempo_map) or a midi_url — and get back how many written notes were heard at the right pitch and time (recall / precision / f1, octave errors, the first missed notes with their beats), the timing error in ms, loudness (integrated LUFS, peak dBFS, clipped share), any stretch where a note was written but nothing sounds, and a verdict (good / check / bad) with reasons in plain words. doseedo_render_midi results already carry this per take (takes[].check) when the part was given as notes. Method: an independent note transcriber (basic-pitch) — dense chords and very fast runs read less reliably; use it as a screen, and listen to anything marked check. Synchronous (~3–15 s), CPU, no credits. Cancel: not applicable — the result is returned in the submit response; the job is already finished.

audio_url.description: The take: a doseedo result URL as returned, or any public https URL.

audio_key.description: R2 ingest key of an uploaded audio file (from doseedo_get_upload_url / POST /api/upload/r2/ingest-url; starts with "ingest/"). Alternative to audio_url.

notes.description: The notes the take should play, in beats from bar 1 (the rows you sent doseedo_render_midi).

midi_url.description: Alternative to notes: the part as a Standard MIDI File (≤ 2 MiB).

instrument.description: The instrument (a drum/percussion name switches to onset-only matching).

onset_tolerance_ms.description: How far a heard onset may be from the written one and still count (default 50).

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_analyze_midi
tools.description: Check the HARMONY of notes before rendering or placing them: factor a MIDI progression into its sonorities (mode "midi", default — chord-detection-free: each segment of simultaneously sounding pitches reduced to an anchor pitch class + register-exact shape, covered with recurring shape cells) or into chord symbols (mode "chord": one estimated chord per ~2 beats + a corpus-grammar cell cover with a schedule). Input: notes[] (the rows you would give doseedo_render_midi / set_midi_notes) with bpm, or midi_url (a .mid ≤2 MiB: a doseedo result link such as a stem's MIDI, or a public URL). Synchronous (~2–10 s), CPU, no credits. Returns sonorities[] or chords[], cover, cells, compression — read chords[].chord / sonorities[].anchor to confirm the key and progression you intended. Cancel: not applicable — the result is returned in the submit response; the job is already finished.

notes.description: The notes to analyze, in beats from bar 1 (same rows as doseedo_render_midi). Needs bpm.

bpm.description: Tempo of the notes (needed with notes; default 120).

midi_url.description: Alternative to notes: https URL of a Standard MIDI File (≤2 MiB).

mode.description: "midi" (default): sonority / shape factoring. "chord": chord symbols per segment + cell cover.

beats_per_segment.description: mode chord: segment length in beats (0.25–8, default 2).

min_seg_beats.description: mode midi: shortest sonority segment in beats (default 0.25).

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_supervise_cues
tools.description: MUSIC SUPERVISION, for a film whose direction is classical or orchestral: instead of writing every note, each cue is CUT FROM A REAL PUBLIC-DOMAIN SCORE (~1,000 orchestral pieces, Baroque to late Romantic, free to use in a film — no rights holds, no ShareAlike). The search fits each cue: its length to the frame (a passage bent ≤ ~17 % in tempo, cut on a bar line where it must), the cue sheet's turns on the score's own section changes, its hits on real accents, its mode and meter, its level over time (a quiet cue thins a tutti's doublings; the loudest moment lands on the source's own rise), and cues of one piece play fresh bars. SAY WHO PLAYS AND HOW BUSY IT IS, or a quiet piano-and-strings cue is cut from a tutti: instruments = the cue's players (the source plays only its parts for those); density = sparse | moderate | busy | driving, or notes a second; per film, or per_cue. Input: spot_job (the doseedo_spot_video job id — spotter "model" gives each second its level) or cue_sheet; cues (ids, default every score cue); direction {era: ["Baroque"|"Classical"|"Romantic"…], genre, composer: ["Antonín Dvořák"…], mode: major|minor}; prefer {cue: file} = take that cue from an alternative an earlier answer listed. Async: job_id → doseedo_wait_task (~5–60 s; a bad direction, cue or prefer fails at once), CPU, no credits. Result per cue: source {composer, title, licence, credit — the line a CC BY edition asks for}, edit (bars, stretch, cuts), render {score_url, instruments, name} = the doseedo_render_score call that plays it (pass it as is; change an instrument by editing instruments), mix_lufs_offset_db (master the cue at the delivery loudness plus this: doseedo_mix target_lufs), alternatives [{composer, title, file, cost}]. Cancel: the plane has no stop for a running catalogue search — it runs to completion (credits spent), the job ends as canceled and its output is discarded. Only a job still queued at the plane is refunded by the plane's own failure refund.

spot_job.description: The doseedo_spot_video job id (job_…): its cue sheet is read for you (MCP tool only; the jobs API takes cue_sheet).

cue_sheet.description: Alternative to spot_job: a cue sheet {video: {duration}, cues: [{id, kind?: "score", start_s, end_s, suggested_bpm?, turns?: [{time_s}], hits?: [{time_s}], dynamics?: [{at_s, mark}], instruments?: [names], density?}], cue_model?: {level_db_per_s}} — doseedo_spot_video's, or your own cue plan in its shape.

instruments.description: The players every cue is cut for (a cue's own instruments win): "violin", "cello", "piano", "harp", "horn", "strings"… The source plays only its parts for these; an asked instrument it lacks is named on the card (ensemble.missing).

density.description: How busy every cue is, on the parts that play: notes a second, or sparse (~2) / moderate (~4.5) / busy (~8) / driving (~13). Music under speech is sparse.

per_cue.description: {cue id: {instruments?, density?}} — one cue's own players and density.

cues.description: Only these cue ids (default: every score cue, ≤ 40).

direction.description: Steer the choice: era / genre / composer as a name or a list of names (the catalogue's own, e.g. era "Romantic", composer "Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky"), mode "major" | "minor" for every cue.

prefer.description: {cue id: catalogue file}: cut that cue from this piece (a file an earlier answer listed under alternatives).

name.description: Optional: a name for this job's files, e.g. "rainy-loop-3". Every file it returns downloads as <name>_<part>.<ext> (rainy-loop-3_Celesta.wav, rainy-loop-3_rough-mix.wav; one take: rainy-loop-3.wav), so the user can find them. Give each job its own name (a second take: "rainy-loop-3b"). Default: doseedo-<last 6 characters of the job id>.

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_instruments
tools.description: The instrument list — the sound palette: every instrument doseedo can PLAY YOUR NOTES on (doseedo_render_midi) — orchestral strings, brass and winds, guitars, basses, keys, drums and percussion, and World instruments (koto, sitar, banjo, pedal steel, tabla, congas…). Each entry gives the EXACT render call (`call`: instrument, plus timbre_preset where one is needed — a koto is the acoustic_guitar model with the koto timbre), its playable range in concert MIDI pitch, whether it plays chords, its presets (pizz, muted, sax registers…) and a demo render. No args → the whole catalog; query:"warm low brass" / family / culture:"India" (a culture's own instruments: "Indian", "Japanese", "Celtic", "Latin America"…) / pitches:[…] (instruments whose range holds them) / chords:true narrow it; id:"cello" → one instrument in full. Read-only, free, no key needed — read it before writing a part.

id.description: One instrument (id, alias or label, e.g. "cello", "upright bass", "koto") → its full entry: every preset with its own call and range, transposition, aliases, demo, page.

query.description: What the part needs, in words: an instrument ("trumpet"), a family ("woodwinds"), a technique ("pizzicato", "muted") or a register ("low", "bright"). Ranked best-first.

culture.description: Only the instruments that are this culture's own sound — a culture ("India", "Japan", "Middle East", "Celtic", "Cuba", "Mexico", "Brazil", "Americana"…), a word for one ("Indian", "Carnatic", "Irish") or a region ("South Asia", "Latin America", "Europe"). The whole listing names every culture.

pitches.description: MIDI pitches the part uses (concert, 60 = C4) — only instruments whose range holds every one.

chords.description: true = only instruments one player can play chords on.

tools.name: doseedo_generators
tools.description: GENERATORS — music you do not have to write. BAND generators (has: ["band"] — jazz …; more genres are added without a release) write a WHOLE arranged piece in a genre: every part's notes (drums, bass, piano, a lead), its form and changes, for a seed. With generator + bars | seconds, bpm, key, seed, lead ("none" = rhythm section alone, "backing" = the whole backing without the tune) → parts[] ({name, instrument, timbre_preset, notes}), form, changes and the .mid (midi_base64): free, instant, no audio. To HEAR it: doseedo_render_score {generator: {id, seed, bars, key, lead}, bpm} plays that exact piece — you pass no notes — and doseedo_mix {from_job} mixes it in the genre's own style (mix_style: a dub's spring tank and tape echo). A film cue or a song that calls for a generator's genre should use it rather than be composed. DRUM generators — ready-made kits and grooves: each generator is a KIT (recorded one-shots for a genre: doseedo_render_midi plays your drum notes through it when the part's drum_genre names it), a LOOP (a groove written for a seed: doseedo_generate_loop → the audio + its MIDI), or both (house, deep house, tech house, afro house, jackin' house — the list grows without a release, so read it rather than remember it). No args → every generator: id, what it has, the drum_genre words that reach its kit, its loop's tempo, swing and bars. With generator (+ bars, bpm, seed, swing, fills, percussion) → that generator's loop AS MIDI: notes[] [{pitch, start_beats, duration_beats, velocity}] (GM drums) and the .mid (midi_base64) — the SAME groove doseedo_generate_loop plays for that seed, instant, free, no audio: read a few seeds, pick or edit one, then render it (doseedo_generate_loop with the same seed, or doseedo_render_midi with your edited notes) or put it on a session track (set_midi_notes). Read-only, no key needed.

generator.description: A generator id ("deep_house") or genre words ("afro house") → its loop as MIDI. Omit to list the generators.

bpm.description: Tempo written into the .mid, 40–240 (default: the generator's).

seed.description: Which groove: the same seed is the same pattern (default 1).

fills.description: false = no fills at the phrase ends.

percussion.description: Percussion voices, 0–4 (default: drawn by the seed).

seconds.description: A BAND generator: the piece's length in seconds (4–600) instead of bars — a film cue's duration.

key.description: A BAND generator: the key, e.g. "F", "C minor" (default: drawn by the seed).

lead.description: A BAND generator: the lead instrument (one of its leads), "none" for the rhythm section alone, or "backing" for the whole backing a singer is given (every chair but the tune's).

direction.description: A BAND generator: what you want of the piece, as doseedo_render_score's generator takes it — {dynamics: [{at_seconds, level: none|low|medium|high|peak, ramp?}], hits: [{at_seconds, kind?: light|medium|full, who?, stroke?}] (who = only those parts land it; stroke = the one drum of the kit that sounds: kick, snare, rim, clap, hat, open hat, crash, tom, high tom, floor tom), lay_out: [{from_seconds?, to_seconds?, who?, only?}] (who rests: no name = the lead; a part, a family, "rhythm", "all"; no times with who or only = the whole piece), thin: [{from_seconds?, to_seconds?, to?: beats|halves|bars, who?}] (who plays thinner: keeps only the beats / the bar's halves / the bar lines), texture: [{from_seconds?, to_seconds?, who, plays?: held|pedal|pulse|arpeggio|ostinato|walk|stabs|comp|line|four_on_the_floor|backbeat|half_time|light|full, value?, level?}] (what a part plays there — taken from the style's own writing for that part over the same chords, never invented; not applied where the style does not play it), textures: true (the answer lists what each part can play: textures), articulation: [{from_seconds?, to_seconds?, who, style}] (HOW the named parts are played there: legato | staccato | marcato | accent | spiccato | tenuto | portato | espressivo | senza_vibrato … — a passage on their articulation, no note changed; pizzicato, tremolo, harmonics and mutes are another sound, not a style), builds: [{into_seconds, beats?, drop?}], ending: {kind: cut|button|ring|fade|form, at_seconds?, strength?, build?} (build: true = the band builds into the last chord; form = no ending, full level to the last beat; left out = the way the style's records end, a ring-out or a fade over the last few seconds), intro: false, swing: light|medium|hard, solo_swing: straight|light|medium|hard} — YOUR OWN BAND: band: [{instrument, timbre_preset?, name?, chair?}] (who is seated in place of the generator's own players) — and YOUR OWN MUSIC for it to arrange: theme: {notes: [[pitch, beat, beats, velocity], …] (beats from the tune's first bar line), statements?: [{at_seconds, on?, from_beat?, beats?, octave?, transpose?, stretch?, mode?: major|minor (the statement in the parallel mode of the theme's tonic), harmony?: [{on, at: third_below|third_above|sixth_below|sixth_above|octave_below|octave_above}] (parts that play it WITH its carrier at that interval)}]} (the generator's own tune comes out and yours goes in, every note as written — with no statements, wherever its own tune was), changes: "Dm | Bb | Gm | A" (your chords, one cell a bar, as a loop; left out with a theme, the chords are harmonised to the theme). STYLE TRANSFER — song: {melody: [[pitch, beat, beats], …], changes: "C | Am | F | G7" (one cell a bar, the WHOLE song), sections: [{label, bars}], meter?, bpm?, key?, phrasing?} plays YOUR SONG in this genre and keeps it exactly: its length, its sections, its chart bar for bar and every note of its tune from bar one (every pitch, in order, sung in the genre's phrasing: an eighth early where the genre pushes the beat or its band pushes the change, its eighths swung in a swing; phrasing: "as written" keeps every onset exactly); the generator decides only how its chairs play it (lead: "none" = the genre's band without the tune). A melody alone is harmonised; chords alone get the genre's own tune; parts: [{name, notes}] (a MIDI arrangement) is read for its tune and chart. A genre in another metre (a waltz, 6/8, 12/8) plays the song re-metered by the meter-change rule and says what moved. only: "bass" | ["bass", "drums"] returns just those parts — the genre's line for one stem, written with the whole band. SEVERAL STYLES, ONE PIECE — layers: ["<id>" | {id, only?, lead?, band?, seed?, name?}, …] (≤ 3): other generators play THIS piece (its bars, chords, tune) each its own way, beside it — a synth score with a process piece's winds and a baroque continuo; a layer adds no second drums / bass / tune unless asked, one layer may carry the tune (lead), a part both styles have comes back "Pad (ambient)", and a direction naming a part reaches only the style that has it. Times in seconds at this bpm, or at_beats / from_beats / to_beats / into_beats.

tools.name: doseedo_tempo_map
tools.description: Scoring to picture: turn HIT POINTS (a cut, an impact, the title card — as seconds from the cue start or SMPTE timecodes) into a TEMPO MAP that lands each hit exactly on a downbeat (or a beat / an eighth — per hit with hits[].land), staying near your tempo and inside bpm_range. A cue whose pace changes (she runs faster, then stops): give the hit where it changes a bpm, and the map moves to that tempo from there, every hit still landed. An AD or any cue that must hold ONE tempo: fixed_bpm: true (+ max_deviation_bpm, tolerance_ms) finds the tempo and the bar-1 offset (music_offset_s) landing the most hits, and says which ones it could not. Returns tempo_map [{beat, bpm}] to pass unchanged to doseedo_render_midi / doseedo_render_score / doseedo_session_from_stems, and hits[] with the beat, bar and beat-in-bar each hit lands on — write the accent, stinger or change there. Handles 23.976 / 24 / 25 / 29.97 (";" = drop-frame) / 30 / 50 / 59.94 / 60 fps timecode. Pure math: free, instant, no key needed.

hits.description: The moments the music must land on: [{time_s} (seconds from the cue start) or {timecode: "01:00:12:08"} (film timecode, with fps and start_timecode), label?, land?, bpm?}] — land = THIS hit's landing ("downbeat", "beat" or "eighth"; default: the request's land), e.g. the big cuts on bar lines and a quick accent on an eighth. bpm = the tempo FROM this hit on, a new section (the chase at 160 from the cut where she starts running, back to 112 when she stops), until a later hit names another; the range around it scales with it. A bare number = {time_s}.

priority.description: What this hit is worth when not every hit can land (tolerance_ms): "must" for the moment the cue is written to (the reveal, the title, the drop) — the map lands it first and the rest around it; "low" gives way first. Default "normal"; a downbeat hit already outweighs a beat.

bpm.description: The cue's tempo (20–300) — the map stays as close to it as the hits allow.

bpm_range.description: Allowed tempo range [min, max] (default ±12 % of bpm).

land.description: Land hits on bar lines (default), on any beat, or on any eighth — the default for every hit without its own land.

fixed_bpm.description: ONE tempo for the whole cue (an ad, a song-form cue): the solver picks the tempo (within max_deviation_bpm of bpm; default exactly bpm) and where bar 1 sits (music_offset_s, default within the first bar; offset_range_s) so the most hits land within tolerance_ms (default 40). Hits it cannot land come back landed:false with nearest_beat — never an error.

max_deviation_bpm.description: How far the tempo may move from bpm (both modes; in place of bpm_range). A variable map at 124 ±12 % can swing 11+ bpm between hits — 3 keeps it a steady groove.

tolerance_ms.description: SOFT hits (0–250 ms): a hit within this of the grid counts as landed, and one the grid can't reach is reported (landed:false, with nearest_beat and off_ms), never refused. The map is fitted over the whole cue, so it lands the most hits — downbeats and priority "must" first. Every hit then carries error_ms; hit_rate = landed / all. A hit with landed:false gets no accent of its own (an accent between the beats sounds like a mistake).

offset_range_s.description: fixed_bpm: where bar 1 may sit on the cue, [min, max] seconds (default [0, one bar]).

start_timecode.description: Film timecode of the cue's first downbeat (bar 1); hit timecodes are measured from it.

start_s.description: Alternative: the cue start in seconds of film time (informational when hits are time_s).

tools.name: doseedo_get_project_upload_url
tools.description: Get a presigned upload for a DAW PROJECT file (for doseedo_convert_project / doseedo_import_project). Zip a project FOLDER so its audio travels with it — and a .logicx or GarageBand .band, which are folders (macOS packages). SIZE LIMITS: a single PUT takes up to 5 GB; guest and free accounts convert projects up to 2 GB, paid plans up to 12 GB (a larger one is refused as project_too_large with the cap and an upgrade link). Pass size_bytes: past 4 GB (or with multipart:true) you get a MULTIPART upload instead — a part_size, one presigned part_url per part, and the complete step (doseedo_complete_project_upload); each part is retried on its own, so a dropped connection costs one part, not the upload. Single PUT: `curl -sS -X PUT -H "Content-Type: application/zip" --data-binary @project.zip "<upload_url>"`, then pass project_key on. Multipart: `split -b <part_size_bytes> project.zip part.` then for each piece in order `curl -sS -X PUT --data-binary @part.aa "<part_url>" -D - -o /dev/null | grep -i etag` (keep each ETag), then doseedo_complete_project_upload {project_key, upload_id, parts}. Need more part URLs than one answer holds? Call this again with project_key + upload_id + part_numbers.

filename.description: File name including extension, e.g. "Song Project.zip", "My Song.band.zip", "beat.flp", "song.cpr", "Mix.song", "set.dawproject" or "score.mxl".

content_type.description: MIME type: application/zip for zips (default), application/octet-stream for bare project files.

size_bytes.description: The file's size in bytes (stat it). Decides single PUT vs multipart and sizes the parts.

multipart.description: Force a multipart upload regardless of size (resumable per part).

project_key.description: CONTINUATION of a multipart upload: the key the first call returned.

upload_id.description: CONTINUATION: the upload_id the first call returned.

part_numbers.description: CONTINUATION: which part numbers (1-based) to sign now, ≤ 24 per call.

tools.name: doseedo_complete_project_upload
tools.description: Finish a MULTIPART project upload started by doseedo_get_project_upload_url: pass every uploaded part's number and ETag (from the PUT response header; quotes optional). Returns the project_key to pass to doseedo_convert_project / doseedo_import_project. All parts except the last must be the same size (what `split -b` produces). abort:true discards the upload instead.

parts.description: [{part_number, etag}] for EVERY part, in order.

abort.description: true = abandon the upload and free its parts (no project_key results).

tools.name: doseedo_import_project
tools.description: Open an uploaded DAW project (Logic (.logicx.zip), Ableton (.als / project zip), FL Studio (.flp), REAPER (.rpp), Pro Tools (.ptx), Cubase (.cpr), Dorico (.dorico / MusicXML), GarageBand (.band zipped), DAWproject (.dawproject), Studio One (.song) and AAF (.aaf, zipped with its audio) — zip a project folder) as an EDITABLE doseedo session: returns a session_id the session tools then work on (doseedo_get_session → doseedo_edit_session → doseedo_download_session as a native Logic project, or convert that download to another DAW with doseedo_convert_project). The session gets the project's tempo (+ tempo map), meter, markers, and every track with its name, mixer level/pan, color and MIDI notes. AUDIO IS NOT CARRIED: the import reads the project, not its media — audio tracks arrive named and positioned (audio.placements lists each clip's file and beats) and audio.next says how to supply the files. Plugins and summing buses are reported, not recreated. Upload first with doseedo_get_project_upload_url; this call parses the project (seconds to minutes for a big one) — if it answers status:"running", call it again with the returned task_id until it hands back session_id.

project_key.description: R2 key of the uploaded project (from doseedo_get_project_upload_url; starts with "uploads/").

daw.description: The source DAW, when the filename does not say (optional; detected otherwise). Every DAW the converter reads.

name.description: Session name (default: the project's own name).

task_id.description: CONTINUATION: the task_id a previous call returned while the parse was still running.

tools.name: doseedo_get_upload_url
tools.description: Get a presigned upload for your own audio file — or a SCORE (.mid / .midi / .musicxml / .xml / .mxl / .mscz / .mscx → a score_key for doseedo_render_score: send a big score as a file, not as notes in the call). Returns an upload_url (PUT the raw file bytes there, e.g. `curl -X PUT -H "Content-Type: <content_type>" --data-binary @song.wav "<upload_url>"`) and an audio_key to pass to doseedo_separate_stems / doseedo_transcribe / doseedo_cover_song / doseedo_audio_to_session, or to doseedo_add_audio_to_session. A FILM (mp4, mov, m4v, webm, mkv; ≤ 2 GB) uploads the same way: pass the key as video_key to doseedo_spot_video / doseedo_score_to_picture. Formats: WAV, AIFF, FLAC, MP3, M4A/AAC, Ogg/Opus, WebM — all accepted for processing on every plan. Storing audio IN A SESSION (doseedo_add_audio_to_session) keeps WAV/AIFF/FLAC lossless only on Pro+; below Pro+ lossless is not kept there, so send Opus (audio/ogg). Samples/regions for a session that are on this machine need NO upload: use load_quick_sampler_sample sample_path / attach_audio local_path / set_track_clips audio_ref.local_path and run place_local_files after the download. A FILE ALREADY ONLINE (a film an editor exported — Canva, Adobe Express — or any public https URL): pass source_url and doseedo copies it in itself — nothing to PUT; the key comes back ready (≤ 256 MB).

filename.description: File name including extension, e.g. "song.wav", "film.mp4", or "cue.mid" / "cue.musicxml" / "cue.mscz" for a score. With source_url: the name for the copy when the URL names none (its extension decides the type).

content_type.description: MIME type; inferred from the extension when omitted (wav, aif/aiff, flac, mp3, m4a/aac, ogg/opus, webm; a film: mp4, mov, m4v, mkv). Required for any other extension.

source_url.description: A public https URL of an audio file or a film to copy in instead of uploading it (e.g. an editor's export link). Returns the key directly — no upload_url, nothing to PUT. ≤ 256 MB.

tools.name: doseedo_check_task
tools.description: Check an async doseedo task once. Returns current status, and the result (file URLs / notes) when finished. A big result comes back as a brief (each row cut to its deciding fields): parts: ["<name>" or index, …] returns those rows of the job record IN FULL — a render_score part's every receipt, a mix part's strip, rides (every point) and loudness, a supervised cue's full card (parts: ["1M7"]).

task_id.description: The task_id returned by a submit tool.

kind.description: Which job kind created the task — the registry name the submit reply carried (generate_music, generate_sound, generate_loop, cover_stem, edit_lyrics, fill_gap, render_midi, train_instrument, render_score, mix, mix_preset, session_from_stems, spot_video, score_to_picture, sound_design, reframe_video, cover_song, separate_stems, split_soundtrack, transcribe, audio_to_session, convert_project, bounce_session, analyze_song, detect_chords, beat_grid, identify_sound, check_take, analyze_midi, supervise_cues); the short codes (generate, sound, loop, coverstem, editlyrics, fillgap, render, train, score, mixpre, stemsess, spot, picture, sfxd, reframe, cover, separate, soundtrack, session, convert, bounce, analyze, chords, beats, identify, check, harmony, supervise) are accepted aliases.

job_id.description: Alternatively the job_id (job_…) from a submit tool or the jobs API — replaces task_id + kind.

parts.description: Optional, on a finished job: the parts to return in full, by name (as the result names them) or index — e.g. ["Oboes", "Timpani"].

from.description: Optional, with parts naming ONE list of a spot_video cue sheet (scenes, shots, cuts, keyframes …): the first row to return (0-based). A long film's list comes in pages — an answer that was shortened says the next from.

tools.name: doseedo_wait_task
tools.description: Wait for an async doseedo job to finish: polls server-side for up to timeout_seconds (5–50; one call can never hold longer than 50 s), then returns the result or the latest status. If it returns still_running:true, call it again — a submit reply's eta_seconds says how long the whole job usually takes (transcribe ~15 s, a render 1–3 min, audio_to_session ~4 min), so a 3-minute job is three or four calls, not one. A finished job answers with its output, artifacts (pre-signed links) and note.

task_id.description: The task_id returned by a submit tool.

kind.description: Which job kind created the task — the registry name the submit reply carried (generate_music, generate_sound, generate_loop, cover_stem, edit_lyrics, fill_gap, render_midi, train_instrument, render_score, mix, mix_preset, session_from_stems, spot_video, score_to_picture, sound_design, reframe_video, cover_song, separate_stems, split_soundtrack, transcribe, audio_to_session, convert_project, bounce_session, analyze_song, detect_chords, beat_grid, identify_sound, check_take, analyze_midi, supervise_cues); the short codes (generate, sound, loop, coverstem, editlyrics, fillgap, render, train, score, mixpre, stemsess, spot, picture, sfxd, reframe, cover, separate, soundtrack, session, convert, bounce, analyze, chords, beats, identify, check, harmony, supervise) are accepted aliases.

job_id.description: Alternatively the job_id (job_…) from a submit tool or the jobs API — replaces task_id + kind.

timeout_seconds.description: Max seconds to wait in this call (5–50, default 45). Start with the submit reply's suggested_next_wait.

tools.name: doseedo_list_jobs
tools.description: List the jobs this account submitted (generate / render_midi / cover / stems / transcribe / session / convert / bounce / the analyses), newest first — to find an earlier result, check what is still running, or resume after a lost connection. Each row names its artifacts (e.g. ["vocals", "drums", "midi_piano"]); doseedo_check_task {job_id} returns the full result with fresh links. Read-only.

kind.description: Only this job kind (registry name): generate_music, generate_sound, generate_loop, cover_stem, edit_lyrics, fill_gap, render_midi, train_instrument, render_score, mix, mix_preset, session_from_stems, spot_video, score_to_picture, sound_design, reframe_video, cover_song, separate_stems, split_soundtrack, transcribe, audio_to_session, convert_project, bounce_session, analyze_song, detect_chords, beat_grid, identify_sound, check_take, analyze_midi, supervise_cues. Short codes (generate, sound, loop, coverstem, editlyrics, fillgap, render, train, score, mixpre, stemsess, spot, picture, sfxd, reframe, cover, separate, soundtrack, session, convert, bounce, analyze, chords, beats, identify, check, harmony, supervise) are accepted aliases.

session_id.description: Only jobs whose input names this session — a bounce, stems registered into it, a render of one of its tracks (filtered within the fetched page).

before.description: Page cursor: the next_cursor of a previous call.

tools.name: doseedo_cancel_job
tools.description: Cancel a queued or running job. What that stops and refunds depends on the kind — generate_music / render_midi / cover_song: a render not yet on the GPU is stopped and its credits refunded; one already rendering finishes (credits spent), the job ends as canceled, output discarded. audio_to_session: cooperative — stops at the next stage boundary and refunds the build's sound-tool unit (a separation already run stays charged). bounce_session: a bounce still queued never renders (budget refunded); one mid-render has its result dropped. spot_video / score_to_picture / reframe_video: one still queued never starts and one running stops within seconds, refunded either way. separate_stems / transcribe / convert_project: no plane-side stop — the work completes (credits spent), the job ends as canceled and its output is discarded. The synchronous analyses are already finished (409 already_terminal).

job_id.description: The job_id from a submit tool or doseedo_list_jobs.

tools.name: doseedo_account
tools.description: Check the connected doseedo account: plan tier, the monthly credit pool (generation AND DAW conversions draw it), purchased extra-usage credits, storage, and whether it owns Dø Desktop (desktop.licensed: a one-time licence is not a plan, so the tier stays free). Read-only — consumes nothing. Use it before starting expensive work to confirm there is budget.

tools.name: doseedo_quote
tools.description: Estimate what a job will cost in credits BEFORE submitting it, and whether the connected account can afford it right now. Spends nothing. Pass the job (generate_music, generate_sound, generate_loop, cover_stem, edit_lyrics, fill_gap, render_midi, train_instrument, cover_song, separate_stems, split_soundtrack, transcribe, audio_to_session, convert_project, bounce_session, spot_video, score_to_picture, sound_design, reframe_video, analyze_song, detect_chords, beat_grid, identify_sound, supervise_cues, analyze_midi, render_score, mix, mix_preset, session_from_stems, check_take) and the same args you would give the job tool (duration_seconds, models, instruments; for render_midi: notes + bpm / tempo_map or duration_seconds, voice_split / voices, takes — takes are free, voices cost one batch per ~6; for render_score: parts + bpm / tempo_map — planned exactly as the job plans it (lines, player rows, length), and `refused` says when the job would refuse it; render_score {generator} is priced as the generator will PLAY it — the band asks the generator for its piece (free) and its parts are priced, a film arc's bare seat at the section it plays (plan.part_rows: each part's rows)). `account.remaining` is the largest ONE charge the account can pay now: an active first-score grant pays a job it has the credits left for, else the tightest of the hour, the day and the month. The estimate follows the planes' own price table; the gate is authoritative and a refusal names the exact price.

job.description: Which job to price (a doseedo_ tool name or recipe verb is accepted too).

args.description: The arguments you intend to pass to the job tool; only the price-relevant ones matter.

tools.name: doseedo_recipes
tools.description: The named pipelines people actually ask for — stems, session (mix → DAW project), cover, transcribe, generate, render-midi (your notes played by an instrument model), custom-instrument (train your own from a recording), timbre-transfer (your notes, a recording's tone), sound-design (SFX / foley / one-shots), analyze-song (key/tempo/sections/chords), convert, bounce, and the compose-part guide (a part in the session's key at its tempo: analyze → you write the MIDI → place or render it) — each with its inputs, the tool calls in order, outputs, a credit/time estimate and how to VERIFY success from the response. Call with no name for the index (pick by use_when), or with a name for the full recipe. Read-only.

name.description: A recipe name or alias, e.g. "session" / "stems-to-session". Omit to list all.

tools.name: doseedo_list_sessions
tools.description: List the connected account's DAW sessions (most recently updated first) — their ids, names, DAW, and update time. Pages with limit + offset (the response carries total and next_offset); name_contains filters by name. Use a session id with doseedo_get_session and doseedo_edit_session; clean up old ones with doseedo_delete_sessions.

offset.description: How many to skip (default 0) — pass the previous response's next_offset to get the next page.

name_contains.description: Only sessions whose name contains this text (case-insensitive).

tools.name: doseedo_delete_sessions
tools.description: Delete DAW sessions in bulk — a SOFT delete (the sessions disappear from the account and every listing; nothing on the user's disk is touched). Select by ids, or by filters (daw_kind, created_before / created_after, name_contains); filters combine with AND. SAFE BY DEFAULT: without confirm:true this is a DRY RUN that deletes nothing and returns {matched, ids}. Always run the dry run first, show the user the count (and names if few), and call again with confirm:true only after they agree. Never delete sessions the user did not ask to remove.

ids.description: Session ids to delete (up to 500), from doseedo_list_sessions.

daw_kind.description: Only sessions bound to this DAW, e.g. "logic", "ableton".

created_before.description: ISO-8601 date/time: only sessions created before this.

created_after.description: ISO-8601 date/time: only sessions created after this.

name_contains.description: Only sessions whose name contains this text (case-insensitive).

limit.description: Cap on how many sessions one call may match (default and max 1000).

confirm.description: false/omitted = dry run (nothing deleted). true = actually delete — only after the user saw the dry-run count and agreed.

tools.name: doseedo_get_session
tools.description: Read a DAW session as the arrangement an agent edits against: every track with its wire ids (track_id t_…, mixer strip channel_id ch_…), regions in BOTH beats and seconds with their MIDI notes (i, pitch, velocity, start_beats, duration_beats — i is what edit_midi_notes selects by), mixer (volume with dB, pan, mute), plugins with params[{param_id, name, value}] (set_device_param needs param_id) and sampler {mode, sample_seconds, plays_beats, …}, sends/output as ch_b_… ids, buses, tempo_bpm + tempo_map, time_signature + meter_map, key_signature when known, markers (marker_id, beat ABSOLUTE from bar 1), automation lanes, instrument, counts, length — and `sync` with live_edits:true|false + live_edits_reason (will an edit reach Logic now?). Field-by-field map: doseedo_edit_ops_reference {section:"summary"}. BUDGET (never cut mid-JSON): notes come inline when the selected tracks hold ≤200 notes, else regions carry note_count + notes_omitted:true — pass include_notes:true with tracks:[ids] for a track's notes; include_params:false / include_automation:false drop params / points; a result still too big is paginated by track with `truncated` + `next` (the exact args for the rest). Read-only. Pass the ids straight to doseedo_edit_session, or a track_id to doseedo_render_midi {session_id, track_id}.

tracks.description: Only these tracks (track_id t_… or channel_id ch_…; a track name matches too). The rest of the session (tempo, markers, buses, sync) is always included.

include_notes.description: Include MIDI notes. Default: true when the selected tracks hold ≤200 notes in all, else false (regions then carry note_count + notes_omitted:true).

include_params.description: Include plugin params (default true). false keeps param_count only.

include_automation.description: Include automation lanes with points (default true). false keeps a lane count per track.

tools.name: doseedo_edit_session
tools.description: Edit a DAW session with a list of ops (regions, MIDI notes, sampler samples, tracks, mixer faders/pans/mutes, plugins, tempo, markers, key, …): ids and current values from doseedo_get_session, op arguments from doseedo_edit_ops_reference. When sync.live_edits is true Dø Desktop puts it into the user's Logic project (it saves, backs up, closes and reopens the project, ~10–20 s — tell the user); otherwise stored and applied at next open. CONTRACT: every op is validated before anything is stored; a rejection carries a code — unknown_op / unknown_plugin (with did_you_mean), unknown_id (with the valid ids), duplicate_id, forbidden_group, read_only_key — and a reason. atomic (default true): one rejection → NOTHING stored, all rejections listed; atomic:false stores the good ops. RETRY: re-send a timed-out call with the SAME batch_key and it dedups (deduped:true); without batch_key a retry duplicates. Ops apply on the desktop one at a time in order, no per-batch undo — verify with doseedo_download_session (replay).

batch_key.description: A stable id for THIS batch (e.g. "drumkit-build-1"). Same batch_key + same ops on a retry = the same client_op_ids = no duplicates. Always pass one for a build you might have to retry.

atomic.description: Default true: any rejected op means nothing is stored. Set false to store the valid ops and receive the rest as `rejected`.

args.description: The op arguments (see the ops reference).

tools.name: doseedo_edit_ops_reference
tools.description: The catalog of session edit ops doseedo_edit_session accepts, served in views that each fit one answer (never cut mid-JSON). DEFAULT (no args): units, ids, applies, groups, batching/policy, the recipe NAMES and every op as {op, group, applies, summary} — read it ONCE before a build. Then fetch what you need: op:"load_quick_sampler_sample" (or ops:[…]) → those ops in full (args, units, doc; an unknown name gets did_you_mean); section:"recipes" → the full recipes (drum kit from local samples, fix note lengths, one-shots on an audio track, remote sample, submix bus, verify) — copy one instead of discovering op order; section:"ops" → every op in full; "units" / "ids" / "summary" (the get_session field map + workflow + policy + batching) / "all" (fitted, may shorten). Each op says where it lands (applies: live in the open project | next_open | state). Read-only, no key needed.

section.description: Which part of the catalog. Omit for the default overview.

op.description: One op name, e.g. "set_midi_notes" — returns that op in full.

ops.description: Several op names — returns each in full.

tools.name: doseedo_desktop_status
tools.description: Is Dø Desktop running on the user's Mac, and can it put edits into their Logic project? Reports which sessions it holds, how it applies edits (apply_mode "reopen" = save, back up, close, apply, reopen), whether macOS lets it (logic_control), each session's last apply (reopen_results) and its applied cursor. Use it to know whether an edit will reach the project now or wait for the next session open. When it is NOT connected the result says how the user gets and pairs the app, and what still works without it. Read-only.

tools.name: doseedo_add_audio_to_session
tools.description: Add an audio file to a session — from a public URL (a doseedo-generated song, a separated stem, any https audio) OR from a LOCAL file you uploaded (doseedo_get_upload_url → PUT the bytes → pass the returned audio_key here). Ingested server-side and returned as a sha256 you then use: place it on a track with attach_audio, or load it into a Quick Sampler with load_quick_sampler_sample {track_id, sample_path: "<the sha>"} (bakes into the exported .logicx, no desktop needed — the drum-pack/sample-swap path). Give audio_url OR audio_key.

audio_url.description: https URL of the audio — any public URL, or a doseedo result URL from a job (pre-signed links work as-is; no key needed).

audio_key.description: audio_key from doseedo_get_upload_url after you PUT a local file to its upload_url (a file from the user's disk, e.g. a drum-pack WAV).

tools.name: doseedo_bounce_session
tools.description: Bounce a session (or specific tracks) to audio on the user's Mac — Dø Desktop renders them in the background WITHOUT the user opening the DAW (engine "headless"): each AUDIO track's regions as the arrangement places them, from bar 1, through the track's third-party Audio Units. Logic's own plug-ins and instrument/MIDI tracks render only inside Logic: each stem names the plug-ins it does not include (plugins_not_rendered), and an instrument track is reported, not rendered. engine "live" (Logic's own bounce) needs a live Logic connection, which the public Dø Desktop does not have. Each stem says its format: the requested wav/aiff, or "opus" when the plan cannot store lossless (the lossless file is then on the Mac at local_path). A track that could not render is named in the error with its reason. Async: returns a job_id — poll with doseedo_wait_task. The result is downloadable stem URLs. Needs Dø Desktop to run at some point to pick up the job; until then it stays queued. No credits (rendered on the user's machine). Cancel: a bounce still queued never renders (its budget is refunded); one mid-render has its result dropped on arrival.

track_ids.description: Tracks to bounce (t_… ids from doseedo_get_session). Omit to bounce the whole session.

stems.description: true (default) = one file per track; false = a single mixdown.

tail_seconds.description: Extra seconds for reverb/delay to ring out (default 2).

idempotency_key.description: Optional. Any unique string for THIS request (e.g. a UUID). Re-sending the same call with the same key after a timeout returns the same job instead of starting a second one.

tools.name: doseedo_download_session
tools.description: Save a session as a native Logic project (.logicx.zip), rebuilt server-side from the session state — no desktop needed. Returns a short-lived NO-AUTH download_url (plain `curl -o ~/Downloads/…`, no header) plus `replay` = what the build put in the file (per track: kind, Quick Sampler sample + sampler {mode, sample_seconds, start/end, plays_beats}, MIDI note count, audio region count; bundled media; deferred ops the offline build could not synthesize) and `warnings` (e.g. a classic-mode sampler whose notes end before its sample; an unknown sample length). `replay.layout {ok, problems}` is read back from the built file (every region on its own track); `replay.master.plugins` is the Stereo Out chain (ch_master); `replay.not_built` counts the ops of tracks the session later deleted (a reused session builds only what it holds now). Verify from replay/warnings, never by unzipping ProjectData. `place_local_files` (when present) is ACTION-REQUIRED after unzipping — for Quick Sampler samples AND audio regions from local paths: a replay track with audio_source:"place_local_files" or a "NOT bundled" warning means that file is not in the zip until you run those cp commands; then tell the user the project is complete.

tools.name: doseedo_list_plugins
tools.description: List the plugins you can insert on a strip with doseedo_edit_session's add_device op. Returns the stock Logic catalog (instruments + effects, always available) and — when Dø Desktop is connected — the actual plugins installed on the user's Mac (stock + third-party). Insert any of them BY NAME: add_device {channel_id, device: {name: "…"}}.

tools.name: doseedo_create_session
tools.description: Create a new, empty DAW session in the account (a blank project you can then populate with doseedo_edit_session, or target with doseedo_audio_to_session). Returns its session_id.

name.description: Session name.
